TEXT.old:
The Windhelm Letters


The following transcribed letters were recovered from a strongbox found after a fire consumed a house in Solitude in the early part of the 3rd Era. Nobody by the addressed name lived at the home, and it is unknown how long the family had owned the strongbox. The letters are believed to have been written during the reign of Jarl Elgryr the Unminded, who ruled Windhelm in the Second Era and about whom few other records are extant.




My dearest Thessalonius,

I hope this letter reaches you, and finds you well. It is getting more difficult to find paper within the city, but I still save the scraps sent by the city's tax agents. I hope you don't mind a household reckoning on the reverse of this.

Windhelm remains as cold as ever, but nothing compared to the heart of her king. Smoke and revelry rise from the palace daily, while we have little wood or coal to keep the chill off. I fear for the little ones, but they're so brave, having never known any other kind of life. We all speak of you daily, and hope that we may come to see you soon.

Yours, Reylia
____


Dear Thessalonius,

Your last message arrived safely, but the promised gold mentioned within did not. When I mentioned this to the courier, she shrugged and turned to the door with no other word. While hearing from you brings joy to us all, I would caution you to not trust that particular woman again.

The minds of the city grow numb with cold and silence. We starve, and the unminded one makes no appearance, no speech, nothing to succor his people. His wizard has been seen walking the streets of the city at odd hours, visiting homes. I saw him paint some horrid symbol on one door -- it dripped like blood before vanishing like sand in the wind. The next dawn, nobody who lived there still drew breath. I am a friend to one of the scullery maids who was sent to clean out the house. She described the most horrible things to me and the children, but I will spare you the details.

The worst of it is, that was a house that supported the king. If that's what happens to his friends, what will be the fate of the rest of us?

But don't let this shift your mind from its important tasks. We all know you work to free us, and pray for your success and swift return.

Love, Reylia
____


This next letter was scribbled onto a piece of cloth with what appears to be charcoal.


Thess.,

I hope you didn't actually ... [illegible] ... efforts are important, but our sufferings must remain ... [illegible] ... retaliation can be swift and terrible. If you no longer care for me, at least think of your ... [illegible] .... Love always, R
____


Dear Thessalonius,

Weeks go by and we have no word from Solitude. I tell the children that you're simply very busy, but it's getting harder to make excuses for you. If you can no longer send money (and I understand, smuggling anything of value into the city has become a fool's errand), at least send word that you still live and work for the freedom of Windhelm.

As regards your issue that I mentioned previously, worry not. With food shortages being what they are, I have removed it from my concerns.

Always yours, Reylia
____


My dearest Thessalonius,

It was good to hear from you at last. Please forgive the rantings of a starving mind. We have at last depleted the basement stores of food, even with the strictest rationing. I see the little ones' faces growing thin and my heart weeps for them. They are, in some ways, brave. I think they're looking after me moreso than I them.

Please come home. I strongly desire to look upon your face.

R
____


Papa,

Ma said to write you, so we love and miss you. Ma is tired a lot, but has lots of visitors, so we are being good and helping.

Love, Stessl and Shapl
____


Thessalonius,

I don't have much time. The city has finally broken. The gates of the palace will not keep us out. The storming begins soon. I have gathered those who still have a spirit to live, and we are taking our own fortunes to hand. I hope to see you on the other side of this. Pray for us as we once prayed for you.

Your Reylia

TEXT.old:
The Woodcutter's Wife
Volume I

As Told By
Mogen Son of Molag



Legend tells of a woodcutter who built a shack deep within the pine forest. There, he hoped to live in peace with his family.

The woodcutter's family lived well for a time, but without warning, the weather turned bitterly cold and spoiled the harvest. Before long, with their meager supply of food all but gone, the family was starving.

Late one snowy night, a traveler knocked on the cabin door seeking shelter from the biting cold. Always generous of heart, the woodcutter welcomed the stranger into his home, apologizing that he had no food to offer.

With a smile, the traveler cast off his cloak to reveal the garments of a mage. As the woodcutter and his family looked on, the mysterious visitor reached into his satchel and withdrew a scroll tied with a silver ribbon. No sooner had the wizard unfurled the scroll and read the words aloud, when a great feast appeared from out of thin air. That night, nobody in the woodcutter's cabin went hungry.

Day by day, the snow piled up. Every night, the mage produced another scroll from his bag and read the words, each time summoning a new feast. On the fifth night, the woodcutter's wife awoke her husband to confess her mistrust of their magical guest. Surely, she argued, there was some price to pay for the magical feasts that everyone enjoyed night after night.

The woodcutter would have none of it. After nearly dying from the lack of food, his family was eating well. The divines had sent them a gift, he explained, and it was foolish to question their wisdom.

But the woodcutter's wife would not be persuaded. Every night, she grew more fearful and more desperate. She was certain that the family had entered into a devil's bargain, and the time would soon come when the mage would ask for something unspeakable in return for his gifts.

While everyone in the cabin slept, the woodcutter's wife snuck out of bed and took her husband's axe in hand. She crept into the traveler's room and with one swing, lopped off his head.

Suddenly, the wizard's disembodied head awoke. His eyes opened wide and when he beheld his maimed body, he let forth a terrible cry.

Awakened by the horrified scream, the woodcutter and his children rushed into the room and gasped at the terrible sight of the decapitated mage.

With his last gasp of breath, the traveler laid a fearful curse on the woodcutter's wife. After her mortal death, she was damned to rise once again and walk the woods alone only to burn at the rising of the sun.

To this day, those who walk the pine forest late at night tell tales of a weeping woman glimpsed between the trees. She carries a bloody axe, the stories say, and is terrifying to behold.

TEXT.old:
Xahxes' Gift: The Reachman Creation Myth

The following is a recording of Kervena, a Reachman matriarch of Old H'roldan. Transcribed by Janus Sarvenelus, agent from the Imperial Office of Reachmen Affairs. Old H'roldan. 3 Suns Height 3E 412

Part 1: The Trickster

And so it was upon the Void Steppes that Anu did sprout from the ground like a Wrothgarian grape. Great was his shapeless form as he quickly consumed and merged with his world-hearth, allowing the creation of the Substance. Pleased with his work, Anu shouted (no, not THAT type of "shout") Anui-El into being with songs of clattering and praise. Yet it was a confusing time for substance-son relationships, one of wandering and sore feet. Journeys of myth-making and unfulfilled revelations bore down on the spirit of Anui-El, so Anu as any good father would did hew him in two, thus forming the terribly beautiful Dragon of Temporal Heart, Auri-El. With their travels, Auri-El brought stability to the land, time with his graceful gait, and the Empty Grains bore fruit and became Gods. Mah-Ra, Zeyht of the Grasses...

...And Sheor. [The narrator at this time makes the sounds associated with a stomach ache. This is a customary and (according to Kervena), a very important part of the myth]

TEXT.old:
Xahxes' Gift: The Reachman Creation Myth

The following is a recording of Kervena, a Reachman matriarch of Old H'roldan. Transcribed by Janus Sarvenelus, agent from the Imperial Office of Reachmen Affairs. Old H'roldan. 3 Suns Height 3E 412

Part 2: Sheor the Tusked-Trickster

Now let me tell you of Sheor, also called the Tusked-Trickster. Sheor was trusted with the important duties of a scout and spent his days mapping the Steppes ahead of the tribe alongside his companion and lover, Kyne. In their seclusion did thoughts of menace manifest betwixt their rutting (who influenced the other I cannot say). It was on one night in a time without nights that The Accursed Two returned to the Celestial Camp.

"Holy hosts, I bring to you a mind of revelatory power. I mean to bring Mortality to Substance and I require the assistance of my brothers and sisters! Kyne herself has laid the foundation of our proposition. Heed her!"

So it was that many of the gods participated in the creation of Nirn, like Magnus Sun-Shaped, who worked with Kyne in the shaping the basis of the new reality. These beings would become the aedra. Those who sat and watched their brothers and sisters and did nothing (save the Funny-Man, who yelled and yelled for Zeyht to invent cheese) became the daedra.

It was just before their creation was finished that Sheor spoke once more:

"Brethren! We are but on the cusp of reaping the benefits of our toiling. I ask you to sing with me in celebration!"
ON THIS AUSPICIOUS DAY OF DAYS
SHEOR ASKS HIS EQUALS FOR THREE GIFTS
HE SHALL NAME THEM WITH HEART AFLUTTER:
LET THE DAWN BECOME NEW LIKE NO OTHER DAWN BEFORE
LET THE CORPSE OF THE OLD AND CYNICAL FORM THE FOUNDATION OF THE NEW AND HOPEFUL
AND LET NIRN BE TORN FROM THE MIND OF THE ARTISAN
AND BE MADE WHOLE INCARNATE
NE NU-MANTIA; ALTADOON LORKHJ

Then something horrible happened.

In the creation of this world, the aedra found themselves unable to move their tents and their herds of spectra refused to leave, mucking up the place with bleating. Worse yet, our ancestors were cursed with this mortality (this is why we tell our children to hold back tears when they scuffle their knees, to not grant the Trickster his due). The daedra watched on in a combination of envy, horror, and amusement at the expense of their kin.

"Why have you done this, brother?" cried Zeyht, his mouth spilling forth with locusts.

"You desire my motivations? Know this, for our children shall not! For-"

Yet Sheor was unable to complete his rambling diatribe, as Orc-Friend Trini himself set himself upon the traitor, pummeling him into theological particulates.

TEXT.old:
Xahxes' Gift: The Reachman Creation Myth

The following is a recording of Kervena, a Reachman matriarch of Old H'roldan. Transcribed by Janus Sarvenelus, agent from the Imperial Office of Reachmen Affairs. Old H'roldan. 3 Suns Height 3E 412

Part 3: The Execution of Sheor

After learning of the betrayal by Sheor Tusked-Trickster, Auri-El in his righteous fury, threw the jaundiced fiend into a pot of scalding ethers, as the rest of the gods tried to make sense of their condition. There was much weeping, especially from Water-Mother Mah-Ra, whose tears filled what would become the Bjoulsae, the lifeblood of our people (Do not let the Nords fool you, she was crying for being cursed with mortality, not for her supposed "husband").

The Trickster goaded the head of our pantheon, spitting, sputtering, and muttering foul aphorisms (not worthy of remembrance).

"Have I not a right to a trial? Do I not have the right as any of you would?"

"Do not waste our time, fiend," said Orc-Friend Trini. 'Your crimes are laid bare and no justification could set things to right. Now is the time for thinking of what to do with such a beast as you!'

"May you be eaten alive by demons dressed as maidens!" Sheor snarled, with fury in his eyes.

Orc-Friend Trini, fed up with such rampant display of irreverence, plucked out the heart of Sheor to stop his mewing (an easy feat, for he, like all Nords, was shallow hearted) and let his cursed organ fly to the land of Dwemereth, where the only people who hate the snowmen as much as us Reachmen dwell.

What fate befell Kyne? Well, let me tell you, stranger. In seeing her partner put down like the rabid skeever he was, she let out a furious scream and wailed over Sheor's corpse, holding him close to her bosom. Seething and bubbling, her body lost its form, becoming the Storm, growing ever larger amongst the tribe.

Facing the wrath of a goddess with naught but destruction in her heart, Auri-El pleaded to father Anu, but his cries were drowned out by the thunderous maelstrom of Kyne. Our gods were swept up in that tumult.

TEXT.old:
Yngol and the Sea-Ghosts



Masser and Secunda passed over Ysgramor's people as their fellowship landed in long-boats upon the rocky shores of Hsaarik Head on their journey from Atmora to Mereth. Boats littered the coast, but Ysgramor did not count his kin, Yngol's among them.

Ysgramor commanded the sea-ghosts to surrender his kin, and a great gale darkened the sky. The seas thrashed and churned, and a wrathful storm appeared. Ysgramor took up the oars and rowed into the storm alone.

Upon the Sea, Ysgramor wrestled the sea-ghosts, and the storm carried him along the jagged coast. Two fortnights passed without relief, until finally the storm broke. Come the next dawn, Yngol's long-boat was found in the icy surf, but the vengeful sea-ghosts had already taken Yngol and his clansmen.

In his terrible grief, Ysgramor slew a dozen dozen beasts and burned them in honor of his fallen kinsman. A barrow-hill was dug in the Atmoran tradition, and Yngol was laid to rest with rites and honors among his clansmen far below the rocky face of Hsaarik Head, the first Children of the Sky to perish in Tamriel.

TEXT.old:
The Origin of the Ash Yam
by Cantur Caelmoryn



The origin of the name "ash yam" seems deceptively simple: it is a species of yam domesticated and cultivated in the ashy steppes of Morrowind. This agricultural practice has assumedly gone on for hundreds of years, ever since the antecedents of the Dunmer arrived from the Aldmeri domains of old. I have made a study into the taxonomy of the ash yam however, and come upon surprising results. Ash yam is not a geographical or botanical term, but a cultural one.

My first contact for my study was with a Redoran landowner located south of Blacklight. In between bellowing at his sparring sons to train harder, this worthy individual related to me an astounding fact: there are more than fifteen different varieties of ash yam, each with their own distinctive shape, color, and (if the culinists are to be believed) flavor. All of these species are capable of being crossbred, leading to hundreds of more varieties and plenty of confusion to more amateur horticulturalists than such esteemed personages as myself. When he learned of my interest in the ash yam, this Redoran landowner invited me to dinner at his liege lord's manor.

As I sat down to dinner with his family, a highly ceremonial affair involving more than fifty people variably related by blood or by oath, I witnessed a surprising ritual. Beside each plate was a small earthenware pot of ash. Before touching their meal (an elaborate affair of nix hound steak garnished with scrib jelly, a side of a cheese-like substance the locals call scuttle, and of course, grilled and basted ash yams) I watched in astonishment as each Redoran individual placed a pinch of this ash on the tongue and invoked the names of their ancestors. This was followed by political and familial banter as the worthy family consumed the rest of the ash, a ritual every single one of the attendees completed before digging into their meal.

I was to learn the reason for this strange custom several hours after dinner, wherein I threw up most of the ash yams in front of my sympathetic host. He explained to me then that some of those fifteen species of ash yam mentioned before are poisonous. There is a compound in them that causes nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and the runs, and it can be distilled down into a popular toxin used in dispensing Redoran political justice. He said that ingesting the ashes purifies one from this poison, hence the peculiar ritual I had witnessed earlier that evening.

The next eve, I again sat down to dinner with the family. Someone had informed the cook of my indiscretion the earlier evening, and the servant was kind enough not to embarrass my constitution again by serving me the ash yams. The family was surprised, therefore, when I asked for the ash yam dish as well as presenting my procurement of a portion of their consecrated ash.

I was expelled from this Redoran household a few days later, but I am pleased to report that I never again suffered from ash yam indigestion so long as I remembered to ingest at least one measure of ash salts prior to my meal. I have thoroughly studied the alchemical aspects of this matter, and have reason to believe that a handful of fine clay could be used to much the same effect. I would highly suggest this latter approach if the reader finds themselves traveling in Morrowind, so they do not risk offending their host by pilfering too much ash from the family's shrine before dinnertime.

TEXT.old:
NAVY PATROL ATTACKED, CAPTAIN KILLED

The Monitor has learned that the Navy recently suffered a grievous and unprovoked attack by an unknown assailant not a day's sail from Anvil. According to an anonymous Navy source who claims to have experienced the attack firsthand, the Imperial vessels TEM Brinerunner and TEM Surfrunner were caught unawares by aggressive enemy vessels while on patrol in the northern Blue Divide. Shockingly, these mysterious attackers were able to overwhelm the two unprepared patrol ships, resulting in the sinking of Surfrunner with all hands. Captain Rulan, commander of the vessel, is among those presumed killed. Per the anonymous source, Brinerunner took heavy damage but was able to narrowly outrun the attackers and return to Anvil.

Fort Telodrach declined to share details on the circumstances surrounding the disaster at sea. According to Navarch Tiledorus Cadmerius' aide-de-camp, Ensign Anandaya, "West Navy patrols routinely encounter brigands, pirates, smugglers, and other such troublemakers while underway, all of whom face swift Imperial justice. The details of individual deployments are a matter of Imperial security and shall not be disclosed."

Adraria Lethris, overseer at the Anvil Shipworks, has confirmed that TEM Brinerunner is indeed in dry dock. Lethris declined to offer further comment.

GOLD ROAD TO UNDERGO REPAIRS

Fort Heath sources confirmed that repairs will be made to the Gold Road between Anvil and Kvatch over the coming months. Legion-supervised crews will be deployed to locations most in need of repair and tasked with filling potholes, replacing missing paving stones, and digging new drainage ditches where necessary.

Travelers are asked to give repair crews space and not to interfere with the execution of their duties. Alternative routes may be temporarily advised.

SMUGGLERS RETURN TO THE NEAR ABECEAN

With Duskwatch Keep now mothballed and West Navy patrols restricted to the main trade routes, the isles of the inner Abecean Sea are once more playing host to a criminal rabble. Rumors of petty smuggling outfits have emerged from the Strident Coast all the way to the mouth of the Brena River. Most concerningly, local sources report that a sophisticated smuggling ring now operates brazenly from somewhere on Stirk Isle, posing a danger both to Charach citizens and to ships plying the routes north of the island.

The Monitor has confirmed similar stories from coastal cities around the Empire, many of which are now feeling the effects of the Imperial Navy's ill-advised decision to shutter several coastal forts and cut down on patrols along critical trading routes. It remains to be seen whether the West Navy's Navarch, Tiledorus Cadmerius, will hold to this disastrous course of action.

BRUSH FIRE BURNS ACRES OF STRIDENT COAST

A lightning strike recently ignited a conflagration near the Anvil-Sutch border, burning the dry shrubland and many trees. The blaze temporarily halted all travel along the western Gold Road while Legionnaires from Fort Heath and the Sutch-Anvil border post worked to contain it.

The wildfire seems to have burned for two days and nights before being extinguished by rain. Although no property was damaged, the disruption to trade highlights the importance of sound Imperial infrastructure to the economic vitality of the Oloman kingdoms of West Cyrodiil.

VALENWOOD CITY PETITIONS FOR ROYAL AID

A Wood Elf diplomatic mission has arrived in Anvil to lobby Goldstone for aid in rebuilding the Valenwood city of Woodhearth, which was grievously damaged by forces of the Summerset Isles during the War of the Blue Divide some three decades ago. The chief envoy, Sirethal Palinis, spoke briefly to the Monitor upon debarking in the Port Quarter, whereupon he stressed the difficulties endured by his countrymer in recent years since the sack.

The Woodhearth delegation was likely drawn to Anvil as a result of Queen Millona's well-publicized charitable initiatives, including programs of bridge construction along the Naharine River and royal support for benevolent institutions like the Saint Naharine Sailors' Home and the Hostel of Saint Rosunius. Nevertheless, financial support for an overseas realm may not enjoy the same support within the walls of Goldstone.

IMPERIAL PRINCE MAKES SURPRISE VISIT TO ANVIL

His Imperial Highness Prince Enman Septim has arrived in Anvil unannounced in a visit that appears to have caught Goldstone authorities by surprise. The Prince and his entourage are expected to accept the customary submissions from the Queen at Goldstone and conduct an inspection of the facilities at Fort Telodrach, though it is unclear when these visits will take place. Enman arrived in customarily resplendent style aboard the Imperial sky skiff TEM Parhelion, which will be docked at Goldstone's Garrison Tower for the duration of the Prince's visit.

The Prince's unexpected visit may disrupt the Kingdom's plans to commemorate the third anniversary of the failure of the so-called Benirus Plot, which many speculated would be marked by a new round of royal donations to local religious orders and charitable institutions.

HADRACHS TO SIT OUT NEXT ELECTION

The poor fortunes of the Hadrach family have continued, according to a new report from the Monitor's Garden Quarter correspondent, Nalen Tanicus. In a shocking admission, Akaterina Hadrach confessed to being unable to pay off a myriad of debts or retain her household staff. Pressed further, Hadrach admitted that in her current financial straits, with only a Navy pension as income, she will be unable to contest the next royal election or make the customary donative to the Red Treasury.

The Hadrach family, one of Anvil's oldest and most prestigious, fell into disfavor with the Queen after the failed coup attempt of 423. Mykol Hadrach, Akaterina Hadrach's father, supported the late Olen Benirus in his ill-conceived attempt to seize control of the kingdom. While Benirus himself was hanged for his treachery, the Queen graciously permitted the Hadrach family to retain their residence in Anvil, demanding only the imprisonment of the elder Hadrach to secure the family's future loyalty.

With the Hadrach family out of a future royal bidding contest, the Imperial Navy's unqualified support of the Queen is expected to continue.

FORT HEATH IRON MINE PRODUCTION SLOWS

A concerning report from a source at Fort Heath indicated that the venerable mine is approaching the end of its viable lifetime. Per the source, who declined to give their name or rank, Fort Heath's gargantuan mine complex has seen its output steadily decline for the last six years. Though some have speculated that new shafts might be dug deeper below the historic main gallery, the prospect of further iron to be found is wholly uncertain.

Fort Heath's iron has long been essential to the Imperial Legion's steel production, outfitting troopers from High Rock to the Padomaic islands. Legion High Command will no doubt seek a new source in the coming years, though it is unclear if any large untouched iron deposits remain to be mined in Cyrodiil.

SOULREST VETERANS RETURN TO ANVIL

The last of the redeployed Imperial Navy marines sent to support Legion troops in Cape Percar have at last returned to normal duty in Anvil. The uprising in Soulrest, the largest such provincial revolt since the Imperial Simulacrum, temporarily overwhelmed the modest garrison on site, requiring Legion and Navy high command to send reinforcements from the West. These forces crushed the rebellion, driving many of their number into the poisonous interior of Black Marsh.

While some of the Anvil-based troops resented the redeployment, most took it in good humor. Some Navy sailors even seemed to enjoy the excursion, with one telling the Monitor that the uprising offered him the chance to connect with his Nibenese counterparts in the South Navy on spiritual matters.

BRINA CROSS MERCHANT SLAIN

Arahn Kimoi, a Brina Cross merchant with ties to the Sutch trade markets, has been killed in his home by an unknown assailant. Authorities report that Kimoi had been known to ply a contentious trade and occasionally found himself in disputes with other West Colovian businesspeople, but sources claim that these disputes were never violent in nature. The perpetrator of this grisly crime remains unknown, as is their motive.

Nerilius Ludos, captain of the Brina Cross guard, has assured the Monitor that a full investigation is underway. Anyone with information on Arahn Kimoi's untimely death is asked to report to Captain Ludos directly as soon as possible.

MERCHANTS SEEK FUNDS FOR AKAVIR TRADE MISSION

Merchant brothers Domenicus and Bartol Fontanarius spoke with the Monitor to share details of their audacious proposal to organize a trade mission to Akavir. Contact with the far eastern continent has been irregular since the failure of Emperor Uriel V's invasion in the late third century, and Imperial policy has generally discouraged mercantile exchange ever since. This fact, and the colossal distances separating west Cyrodiil from the Uttermost East, have not discouraged the Fontanarius brothers, who sat with the Monitor's Barbona Disenne to discuss their venture. Their interview is transcribed in abridged form below.

B. Disenne: "Thank you for agreeing to discuss this remarkable plan of yours. How did you come by the inspiration for such a scheme?"

D. Fontanarius: "My brother and I are businessmen, madam -- businessmen with a nose for profit. We haven't made it as far as we have in the import business without a keen sense for new opportunities."

B. Disenne: "What makes you so certain that a voyage from Anvil could reach Akavir? Would it not be easier to organize such a mission from Thorn, Necrom, or Archon?"

B. Fontanarius: "I'm sure an educated journalist like yourself knows that the world is round. As the War-Emperor learned to his sorrow, the western coasts of Akavir are inhabited by vicious Tsaesci with little love for Tamrielics and our Empire. By sailing west, we are confident that we can instead trade with the peaceable monkey-folk of Akavir's eastern isles."

B. Disenne: "I assume you have detailed maps of the lands of Yokuda, which lie between us and these faraway isles? It is said that they are quite treacherous."

D. Fontanarius: "I've been well informed by traders from the Far West that the isles of Yokuda are quite placid in modern times, and host only gentle farmers and peaceable merchants. Nevertheless, our crew will be well-prepared to take arms in the event of an attack."

B. Disenne: "On that subject -- what ship do you intend to take west?"

D. Fontanarius: "At this stage, we are seeking a ship capable of the long journey. I'm certain that the famous ports of the Kingdom of Anvil will provide a vessel up to the task."

B. Disenne: "Thank you for your time, gentlemen. May the Goddess fill your sails with her breath. When you get a ship, that is."

EDITORIAL: THE COSTS OF DARK ELF SLAVERY
by Cydne Jouarge

None doubt that the Law reigns supreme in the Empire -- indeed, the Empire IS Law, as the Emperor's coinage and proclamations so often remind us. In the West, the inviolability of Sacred Law is held implicit, and the maxims of Imperial order hold sway throughout public life. This enlightened, civilized consensus holds from Lune to the Nibenmouth, in almost every land of this vast continent. Even the Summersets have been held to account before the light of Imperial Law, and the grim serfdom once common in those lands no longer poisons the human soul.

Only in Morrowind -- impudent, intemperate Morrowind -- does the barbarity of slavery still blight the face of modernity. Only in Morrowind does the law of Tiber Imperator stand silent before the savage law of petty subject fiefdoms. Only in Morrowind does the promise of Alessia and Tiber fall to its knees, gasping for breath in the choking ash of that cruel land.

Some Western defenders of slavery have chosen to depict the Armistice of the last era as itself a shackle around the Imperial wrist, binding and twisting our shared common Law to protect its Dark Elf subjects' pernicious institution. But this is a folly. Imperial Law is upheld by the Imperial Legions, the mightiest fighting force ever assembled. Should justice come to pass, and the Emperor withdraw the provisions of the Armistice, none but the most foolish slavers would dare to contest the Legions' might.

The natural proclivities of man are the foundational principle of Sacred Law, as upheld by centuries of legal tradition. The imposition of slavery on a free Empire is an affront to the dignity of the enslaved and free alike, as those of us who watch helpless as Imperial citizens languish in the chattel pits of Tear or the sweltering plantations of the Thirr must witness with horror the desecration of Imperial Law. Four and a half centuries of this insult must be met with answer -- by the sword, if necessary.

INVESTIGATIONS IN THE KIMOI CASE REACH A DEAD END

The brutal murder of Arahn Kimoi, a prominent Brina Cross businessman, has been solved by the local guard corps with valuable assistance from members of the public. Kimoi, whom sources report had been involved in tense business disputes with various Sutch merchants, was murdered in his manor. Direct evidence from the crime scene led to the identification of the assassin.

Unfortunately for the cause of justice, Arahn Kimoi's assassin, an Argonian stranger not known in the Kingdom of Anvil, was found dead in a room at the Gosha Inn on the border with Kvatch. According to Nerillius Ludos, captain of the Brina Cross guard, the murderer had been attempting to flee east before being cut down herself, perhaps as punishment for the amateurish execution of the late Mr. Kimoi.

With the contractor of Arahn Kimoi's assassin still at large, citizens are advised to take care in public and lock their doors, especially those readers who are engaged in business dealings in the Kingdom of Sutch.

LOCAL BUSINESSMAN ARRESTED ON TREASON CHARGES

The Monitor has been informed that Unsolyo, a Sea Elf clothier in Anvil, has been arrested by the West Navy and imprisoned in Fort Telodrach's dungeons. Ensign Anandaya, an aide to Navarch Tiledorus Cadmerius, stated that Unsolyo was taken in on treason charges, but refused any further comment.

According to anonymous sources within Fort Telodrach, the arrest and prolonged detention of Unsolyo is linked to the recent attack by unknown forces on two Navy cutters on routine patrol in the Abecean Sea. The attack, which saw one ship sunk and another grievously damaged, has raised questions about the safety of the critical sea lanes of the eastern Abecean Sea.

While Sea Elf forces have been known to confront Imperial forces intermittently, a brazen attack on Imperial fleets in Abecean waters would constitute a serious breach of the detente long held between Tamriel and Pyandonea. The arrest of a respected Sea Elf merchant citizen seems to indicate that Navy intelligence has not ruled out this threat.

With piracy on the rise in the Abecean Sea, the arrival of Sea Elf raiders presents a frightening new danger for sailors and traders. The West Navy, weakened by the recent attacks and the Navarch's decision to mothball certain forts, appears unprepared to face this new threat. The arrest of an Imperial citizen on the basis of race with unspecified evidence only highlights High Command's unpreparedness at this critical moment.

LOCAL BUSINESSMAN EXONERATED OF TREASON CHARGES

The West Navy has released the well-known Anvil clothier Unsolyo after his arrest and imprisonment on treason charges. While the details of these charges remain unknown, and Fort Telodrach offered no comment, anonymous West Navy sources linked the Sea Elf's arrest to the mysterious attacks suffered at sea by the TEM Brinerunner and TEM Surfrunner.

Unsolyo, who owns a prosperous shop in Anvil's Marina quarter, never stopped protesting his innocence throughout his imprisonment. Now free, he's indicated a desire to return to normalcy. "I'm an Imperial citizen, and an honest businessman," he told the Monitor's Barbona Disenne. "I'm just glad that nightmare is over."

Despite repeated attempts, Fort Telodrach remains stubbornly quiet about the clothier's imprisonment and subsequent release, and has refused to disclose any new information about the attacks on its ships. The silence of Navy High Command bodes ill for the safety of ships at sea and the rights of Anvil citizens before Imperial Law.

GEOGRAPHICAL SOCIETY CALLS FOR TRAVELERS' TALES

After months of speculation, the Imperial Geographical Society confirmed that it will indeed publish a Third Edition of its much-celebrated Pocket Guide to the Empire.

The First Edition of the Guide, published during the early reign of Tiber Septim, and the Second Edition, published during the reign of Empress Morihatha, made enormous contributions to Imperial unity, bringing readers to far-flung corners of Tamriel during critical moments in Imperial history. That the Society has chosen this moment to publish a new Guide speaks to the importance of the contemporary age and the need to document the modern Empire for a modern generation.

Wolli Antipodine, head of the Society's office in Anvil, has put out a call for travelers' testimonials, particularly those who have visited the recently-opened island of Vvardenfell in Morrowind Province.

ARCHAEOLOGICAL SOCIETY PLUMBS NEW DEPTHS IN GARLAS AGEA

The Imperial Archaeological Society has opened a new excavation site in Garlas Agea, an Ayleid ruin on the eastern fringes of the Kingdom of Anvil. The dig has been much anticipated by the scholars of West Cyrodiil and beyond, who hope that the Society's efforts will shed new light on the many questions that still surround the Ayleids.

"We made quick progress at first, and uncovered a massive spiral staircase that seemed to go downwards forever," recalled Otto, an excavator in the Society's employ. But after a promising start, the expedition stalled when it encountered ferocious opposition from the ruins' denizens. "When we got to some kind of funeral chamber, deep in the ruin, we were attacked by spirits, Daedra, and twisted ancient golems," said Kalana Monilian, another excavator. In response to these attacks, the expedition retreated, setting up camp at the base of the great spiral stair.

Despite the setback, the small excavation crew plans to stay on site to explore other sections of the ruins. Bucynarel, the expedition's leader, remains hopeful. "Garlas Agea was one of the most prominent Ayleid city-states in the Colovian West," she said. "It was said to hold one of the greatest libraries of its time. We won't be turning back until we find it."

According to Bucynarel, success at Garlas Agea would be the biggest breakthrough in Ayleid archaeology since the rediscovery of Hame deep in the jungles of Kavas Rim during the reign of Emperor Cephorus II.

MASQUED CAPTAIN APPREHENDED

The Monitor has confirmed reports from Goldstone that the infamous Masqued Captain has been apprehended by the Kingdom of Anvil. The anonymous outlaw, who has overseen a campaign of piracy and terror in the Abecean for six years, is now imprisoned and awaiting trial in the dungeons beneath Goldstone, according to Lantin Chaskav, captain of the Anvil guard corps. While a trial date has not yet been set, sources in the castle confirmed that delivering the Emperor's justice to the West's most notorious pirate is the Queen's highest priority.

It remains unclear how the Masqued Captain was captured, and whether or not his identity has yet been revealed. Chaskav did confirm that the 10,000 septim bounty placed on the Masqued Captain was indeed paid out, though he refused to identify the bounty hunter "for their own protection".

TEXT.old:
MASQUED CAPTAIN ESCAPES CUSTODY

Lantin Chaskav, captain of the guard at Goldstone, confirmed yesterday that the Masqued Captain escaped Kingdom of Anvil custody only a day after his arrest, frustrating a years-long attempt to bring him to justice for more than half a decade of piracy and brigandry.

Chaskav declined to comment on the circumstances of the corsair's escape. However, an anonymous Goldstone source told the Monitor that the castle's state-of-the-art thaumatic disruptor, designed to protect the site from unauthorized teleportation attempts, had been disabled by unknown actors. "The Masqued Captain had help, no doubt about it," the source said. "Whoever got him out knew the castle well, and knew exactly where and when to make their move."

With the Masqued Captain once again at large, all eyes are on the Queen as she considers the Kingdom of Anvil's next steps against this cunning and implacable enemy.

ABECEAN TRADING CO. ACQUIRES WHITE SCARAB CO. IN TITANIC ANNEXATION

After months of preliminary negotiations, the acquisition of the White Scarab Company by the Abecean Trading Company has been finalized in a formal meeting of both companies' boards of directors at the Salthearth manor-estate of Velius Ivrol in the Kingdom of Sutch. The terms of the acquisition preserve the White Scarab Company as a separate firm with its own board of directors headquartered in Sutch, but restructure it as a subsidiary of the larger Anvil-based Abecean Trading Company.

Micella Marin, Director and Chairwoman of the ATC, gave the following statement to the Monitor.

"This merger represents the product of months of diligent, patient negotiations between representatives of both Companies. All involved parties strongly feel that the combined interests of our two firms are stronger as a single whole. Shareholders of both firms should see immediate growth in their investments -- growth which we intend to build upon further in the coming years."

Although Goldstone declined a statement, Queen Millona of Anvil was thought to oppose the two corporations' merger. The Abecean Trading Company, already one of the most powerful companies in the world, is largely controlled by Herrius Thimistrel, the Queen's wealthiest and most influential critic. Thimistrel, who controls a majority of ATC shares but largely stays out of the Company's day-to-day affairs, is thought to be a leading contender for the crown of Anvil in the event of a new royal auction.

EXOTIC DISEASE OUTBREAK IN ANVIL

Goldstone has confirmed reports that five Anvil citizens have fallen ill with Bluepox, a poorly understood and very rare disease. These cases are the first recorded in Anvil in over a century and the most it has ever suffered at once.

While Bluepox is not one of Morrowind's infamously virulent blight diseases, as some feared when it first appeared in the city, Goldstone sources did not provide any alternative explanation for its sudden appearance, merely stating that an investigation into the disease's origin was underway.

Although little about the disease is known for sure, common symptoms of Bluepox are known to include muscle spasms, fatigue, and the development of blue pox spots across the body. Officials have requested that anyone with additional information about Bluepox or the outbreak itself come forward at once, lest the outbreak spread and infect more citizens.

SUMMERSET FOOD IMPORTS CONTINUE TO RISE

Grain and meat futures continue to show growth as Trident Exchange brokers report sustained and increasing demand from the Summerset Isles. The archipelago's burgeoning population, which Census and Excise records indicate is now higher than ever before, seem eager to import Cyrodiil foodstuffs at cheaper cost and in more reliable supply than counterpart goods produced on the Isles.

According to Nalirindo, chairman of Anvil's Chamber of Commerce, this trade in food goods benefits all participants. "It's simple supply and demand," he told Carson, the Monitor's economic correspondent. "The Summerset Isles cannot produce enough food to feed its people. Luckily, the Empire's wise trade policies allow merchants to fill this gap -- and make a profit in doing so." When pressed on the subject of the High Elves' growing dependence on foreign imports, Nalirindo -- himself a High Elf of Cyrodiilic birth -- waved off the concern. "In the Empire, we all rely on trade between the Provinces. Why, I smoked a siyat cigar from Hammerfell just this afternoon. So long as the Legions keep good order on the roads and the Navy keeps good order at sea, the interdependence of the Provinces is an asset, not a liability."

EDITORIAL: THE SAD STATE OF THE IMPERIAL NAVY
by Vasil Richton, Marshal of the River, Kingdom of Kvatch

Students of history know well the feats of the Imperial Navy, from the heroic conquest of the Summersets to the intrepid invasion of the Far East. The brave sailors of five centuries have served their Emperor through tumult and trial, ensuring for generations to come the peace of the seas.

In the light and legacy of such progenitors, today's cardinal fleets are but a pale shadow. The North Navy, renowned in song as the escorts of intrepid polar explorers, now cedes its duties to a rabble of privateers whose longships afflict the traders of Winterhold and Blacklight with the Emperor's blessing. The once-vaunted East Navy has abandoned its shieldforts, leaving the eastern coast of Tamriel to the ravages of Padomaic raiders -- or worse, a new attack from Akavir. The South Navy, long Tamriel's wooden wall against the Sea Elves, has retreated into the redwater Niben. But worst of all is the degradation of the West Navy under its present Navarch, Tiledorus Cadmerius.

Under Navarch Cadmerius' control, the hallowed West Navy has seen itself become merely an appendage of continental actors, its hardy sailors reduced to lackeys for schemers and crooks. West Navy High Command has seen fit to mothball forts guarding the Abecean Sea's most critical trade lanes, keeping ships in port at Fort Telodrach while the merchants of Anvil and Stros M'Kai flee emboldened pirates. Worse yet, the Navarch does nothing while his surrogates play politics in the Kingdom of Anvil and cavort with its queen.

The Emperor must see that the crumbling of the Imperial Navy bodes ill for his Empire. Only a thorough overhaul of its leadership across all four cardinal fleets can now save this respected institution from terminal decline.

NEW TRADING COMPANY EXPLODES IN VALUE AMIDST SERIOUS DOUBTS

Miracle or mirage? The streets of Anvil have been buzzing with talk of the Black Isle Company, a distributor of goods from Vvardenfell island which has made waves off the back of a seemingly endless stock run. The mania surrounding the company has grown to the point where brokers speak of paupers, some with the very clothes falling off their backs, demanding a share of the company in exchange for what little they have to their name. Indeed, to hear some speak of it, the Black Isle Company seems not to be a company at all, but an infinite font of wealth by which one can convert even a small sum into a fortune. This all begs a simple question: what has it done to earn its success?

In an effort to shed light on the situation, the Monitor sat down with a Black Isle Company representative for a few questions. Sadly, answers were not forthcoming. Over the course of the interview, the representative made several fundamental errors about the company's history and failed to provide any coherent image of what, exactly, its day-to-day operations look like -- save that they must be chaotic. How else could it be that the Company's designated spokesperson knows so little about its most basic facets?

It can only be said that the Black Isle Company appears to be all tremors and no eruption; a con job staffed by smooth-talkers who know nothing; in all respects, a sham. And while the Monitor's readers are encouraged to make their own financial decisions, they are also cautioned to remember that what goes up must eventually come back down.

NEW TRADING COMPANY EXPLODES IN VALUE DESPITE ORGANIZATIONAL DEFICIENCIES

Miracle or mirage? The streets of Anvil have been buzzing with talk of the Black Isle Company, a distributor of goods from Vvardenfell island which has made waves off the back of a seemingly endless stock run. The mania surrounding the company has grown to the point where brokers speak of paupers, some with the very clothes falling off their backs, demanding a share of the company in exchange for what little they have to their name. Indeed, to hear some speak of it, the Black Isle Company seems not to be a company at all, but an infinite font of wealth by which one can convert even a small sum into a fortune. This all begs a simple question: what has it done to earn its success?

In an effort to shed light on the situation, the Monitor sat down with a company representative for questions. The somewhat scattered interview that followed painted an image of an ambitious company in the midst of growing pains. Grandiose in its vision, the Black Isle Company has seemingly relegated 'viability' and 'internal consistency' to secondary concerns.

With this in mind, the idea that it could ever succeed should seem laughable. And yet, having not even received its first full batch of goods from Vvardenfell, its potential appears limitless. The high value commanded by Dark Elven commodities in Cyrodiil is no secret. Many a trader has pleaded for the day when the East Empire Company loosens its hold on Morrowind for just a moment. And a growing number believe that it will be the Black Isle Company which finally answers their prayers.

If they're correct, then the concept behind the Black Isle Company is too perfect -- too natural and anticipated and 'right' -- to fail, no matter how mismanaged it is. The Company's leadership certainly seems eager to test this theory. But if, on the other hand, the Black Isle Company is merely an economic enterprise, then its fundamentals simply do not bear out against the public's enormous expectations for it.

NEW TRADING COMPANY EXPLODES IN VALUE WITH INNOVATIVE BUSINESS STRATEGY

Miracle or mirage? The streets of Anvil have been buzzing with talk of the Black Isle Company, a distributor of goods from Vvardenfell island which has made waves off the back of a seemingly endless stock run. The mania surrounding the company has grown to the point where brokers speak of paupers, some with the very clothes falling off their backs, demanding a share of the company in exchange for what little they have to their name. Indeed, to hear some speak of it, the Black Isle Company seems not to be a company at all, but an infinite font of wealth by which one can convert even a small sum into a fortune. This all begs a simple question: what has it done to earn its success?

In an effort to shed light on the situation, the Monitor sat down with a company representative for questions. What resulted was a dive into the inner workings of one of the most interesting newcomers to Cyrodiil's corporate world. One of the most common concerns regarding the Black Isle Company is the legality of its operation, given the East Empire Company's charter over all Morrowind. The BIC skirts this by using the EEC as a middleman, purchasing bulk quantities of goods at a discount and selling them piecemeal throughout Colovia. This process, which streamlines the bureaucratic morass associated with buying from the EEC, allows the BIC to sell Dark Elven goods at lower prices while still making a profit.

It is this innovative new business model which has resulted in the Company's sky-high stock price. Indeed, even before the first shipment of goods has arrived from Vvardenfell, several businesses throughout Colovia have announced their intention to source their products through BIC representatives.

While the Black Isle Company's rise has been unprecedented, the competence of its employees and forward-thinking vision of its leaders make it seem less a fluke than the long-theorized confluence of several factors in an enterprise much greater than the sum of its parts -- one which is no doubt poised to change the corporate landscape forever.

EDITORIAL: QUESTIONS SURROUND SUTCH KING'S DEATH
by Solvus Orrich, royal steward of the Kingdom of Anvil

Amidst the pomp of young King Attrebus' ascension to the throne of the Spire City, many are still seeking the truth of his predecessor's fate. King Attrebus' court has told all that the late King Cirellus of Sutch died tragically in a hunting accident, a story confirmed by the loyal knights who now hold high positions in the Court of the Gorge.

King Attrebus, who grew up a modest cowherd, rose to the succession by word of the childless King Cirellus before his death. Although the late King trusted his chosen successor, many now wonder if this trust was misplaced. King Attrebus' wife, the now-Queen Enide, is widely rumored to have ties to the Kali Mes insurgent organization. One can only imagine the damage such an asset could do in her new seat, if these rumors are true.

Perhaps young King Attrebus means to do good, and will ignore the incendiary whispers of his queen. Perhaps they are both complicit in a tragic conspiracy to depose their old benefactor. Either way, the knights of Anvil must stand a watchful vigil against unrest from the north.

TRADE SHIP LOST IN SUSPECTED PIRATE ATTACK

Charach sources report that Emperor Cassynder, a trade ship bound for the port, never arrived as scheduled. It remains unclear where and when the ship was lost, but as the days continue to pass, the vessel's owner, Theseus Caperno, has lost all hope in its arrival.

The loss of the Emperor Cassynder is only the latest in a long series of private trade vessels which have failed to reach their destinations in recent months. The withdrawal of the West Navy from its outpost of Duskwatch Keep on Stirk Isle and the reduction in naval patrols has left the trade lanes of the Near Abecean almost entirely unprotected. Pirates and smugglers have seized the opportunity, most of all the infamous Masqued Captain. While those responsible for the sinking of the Emperor Cassynder remain unknown, the ultimate culprit is clear: Navarch Tiledorus Cadmerius, whose irresponsible decision-making has left the honest merchants of the Abecean Sea completely at the mercy of criminal opportunists.

LOST MAGE FOUND ALIVE DEEP BENEATH ABECEAN SEA

In a shocking twist on a weeks-old cold case, the missing mage Divides-To-Iron has been found alive by a fellow member of the Mages Guild. The Argonian left on a solo expedition into a seafloor Ayleid ruin near the Mykoi Isles of the northern Abecean Sea, but failed to return at the expected time.

According to reports from the Mages Guild, Divides-To-Iron became trapped in a one-way passage deep inside the Ayleid ruin, which he identified as "Nagaiarelle". When a Mages Guild %PCRace finally found him, the mage had been living on a diet of fish and a dwindling supply of fresh water for more than three weeks. Because of his unique Argonian physiology, Divides-To-Iron was able to breathe in the ruin's depths, though the salt water made this exhausting.

Despite these difficulties, Divides-To-Iron appears to have taken his ordeal in good humor, telling the Monitor he "loves seafood". The Mages Guild made no comment on its future plans regarding explorations of Nagaiarelle.

DIBELLANS IN DISARRAY AS FACTIONALISM GRIPS FAITH

The fate of Anvil's largest and most prominent temple appears much in doubt as competing internal factions continue to vie for control of the Great Faith of Dibella. Having already cast aside the cult's long-standing hedonistic tenets in favor of a new dogma preaching ascetic purity, Primate Hiral Varollus has displayed no sign of letting up the pressure. New restrictions have been imposed on the usage of the Sacred Baths in the Temple of Dibella Estetica, and the Faith has retracted all of its former charitable contributions to the Guild of Courtesans. The Primate has herself relocated from the Faith's primary cathedral in Cyrodiil City to the larger temple in Anvil, where she has cloistered herself behind a cadre of spiritual advisors and refused to take any visitors.

Traditionalists in the cults of Dibella have not given up the fight. Several sources at the Temple of Dibella Estetica spoke with the Monitor on condition of anonymity, revealing a temple wracked by infighting and bureaucratic friction. With shaven heads becoming an unofficial badge of the ascetic movement within the faith, one Dibellan source claimed that those who have kept their hair have been targeted by punitive demotions and disproportionate penalties for petty offenses. Those who have embraced the ascetic line, meanwhile, have seen themselves rocket to high positions within the clergy, even leapfrogging their non-ascetic former superiors in some cases.

The Temple of Dibella Estetica has long been a destination for pilgrims from across the Imperial Province and beyond. It is unclear how the ongoing internal conflict will impact visitors from outside the clergy, but pilgrims are advised to take caution when visiting the Temple not to offend either the dominant ascetics or their hedonist rivals at this time.

URRI THE RED ACCEPTS LETTER OF MARQUE

Traders and sailors in Anvil's Port Quarter were taken by surprise by the arrival of the infamous pirate galleon Heat Lightning to the city. Goldstone sources confirmed to the Monitor that her captain, Urri the Red, has accepted a letter of marque from Queen Millona, bringing her much-feared skills into the service of the Kingdom of Anvil. The Nord corsair, who had previously been the target of high bounties in Anvil, Rihad, and Hegathe, received a pardon for her crimes in exchange for becoming a privateer and swearing a solemn oath to cease all attacks on peaceful trade ships.

Heat Lightning has long been a feared sight for sailors on the high seas. Urri the Red burst onto the pirate scene eight years ago with her defeat of the fearsome Minna Amarant, whose Sapphire Squall had afflicted Stros M'Kai and the Chain for decades. Urri proved less provocative, but far more cunning than "Mad Minna", thriving in the violent world of Abecean piracy for years, while less skilled captains were deposed by the ascendant kingpin of the pirate world, the mysterious Masqued Captain.

Letters of marque were once common in the Abecean Sea, but have largely fallen into disuse as local rulers came to rely on the Imperial Navy to protect their shores. The West Navy's recent decision to draw down its force projection in the Near Abecean has no doubt informed the Queen's decision to pardon and deputize such a notorious pirate as Urri the Red.

FIGHT PIT PHENOM FINISHES FIRST IN FABULOUS FASHION

The rapid ascent of the Pilgrim in the Abecette Casino's world-famous arena has taken Anvil by storm and caused a great deal of tumult in the betting markets. Emerging from complete obscurity only recently, the Pilgrim has convincingly dispatched a succession of challengers, including the crowd favorites Harge the Large, the Corsairs, and Takhur the Terrible. To the delight of the crowd, the Pilgrim ended their historic run in the season's championship bout against the previous champion, the Nightingale, a contest which saw over nine million septims wagered.

While it is unclear what the future holds for this popular new fighter in coming seasons, the Pilgrim's unprecedented ascent to the very pinnacle of the sport has already earned them a place in pit fighting history for a generation.

DRUG KINGPIN ARRESTED IN ANVIL

Skingrad-based drug kingpin Za'Rabi has been arrested in Anvil's Little Arenthia neighborhood, and is now imprisoned and awaiting trial in Goldstone. The Skingrad-based Khajiit drug lord was caught in a complex sting operation which also involved several other drug traffickers operating in Anvil and its environs. Reymanus Pelelius, Marshal of the Strident Coast, commended the city guard for their efforts and thanked %PCName, a new recruit to the Anvil constabulary, for their critical role in the sting operation.

Skooma addiction has become an increasingly serious issue in Anvil in recent years, and locating the drug's primary importer has long been a priority of the city authorities. The source remained a mystery until a local merchant named Straler Loronus turned himself in, claiming to be the city's primary skooma manufacturer. Loronus, citing the fatigue and stress inherent to his criminal lifestyle, offered to collaborate with the city authorities in the operation to catch Za'Rabi.

MARAV FARMERS STRIKE RESOLVED PEACEFULLY

A tense situation in Marav was resolved after mediation from Kingdom of Anvil representatives working for Reymanus Pelelius, Marshal of the Strident Shore. The people of the small farming village, which lies just across the Naharine River from Anvil, had taken Reeve Keitius Nobius captive and stopped all work in protest of Imperial tolerance of slavery in Morrowind. Marav's farmers demanded an ongoing subsidy from the Crown in exchange for resuming work and releasing the Reeve.

The standoff was resolved by a negotiated settlement arranged by the Kingdom of Anvil's representative, a capable %PCRace working on behalf of Marshal Reymanus Pelelius. While the demand for an ongoing subsidy was denied, the Kingdom agreed to pay a one-time sum to compensate the Marav farmers for their market losses to slave-grown imports. The Marshal also promised the farmers that their interests would be advocated for by the administration more actively going forward in the Kingdom's negotiations with interprovincial firms and the Empire's trade administrators.

Reeve Nobius, who was sympathetic to the villagers' cause, urged the Kingdom to take no retaliatory action. "The people of Marav are hard-working and decent, and they felt that they had no other way to be heard," he told the Monitor. "When Nibenese monopolists import slave-grown food from Morrowind at low prices, Colovian farmers simply can't compete."

TEXT.old:
QUEEN MILLONA DEPOSED, NEW QUEEN CROWNED

Goldstone sources have confirmed reports that Millona Pelelia Conomorus, Queen of Anvil since 3E 407, has been removed from power. While the circumstances surrounding her fall remain unclear at this time, there can be no doubt that the Kingdom of Anvil is now entering a new and unexpected era. A spokesperson for Goldstone confirmed that Queen Millona remains safe and unharmed.

According to reports, Akaterina Hadrach made the customary royal donative to the Red Treasury shortly after Queen Millona conceded the throne, and in doing so thus claimed the Trident Crown. The new Queen Akaterina has urged calm and patience while her administration takes control of the realm, and has promised that her predecessor's most important investments will be maintained. The Kingdom's Marshals, Reeves, and guard captains, including Queen Millona's brother Marshal Reymanus Pelelius, are expected to retain their positions, at least for the moment.

Queen Millona, who entered her office as the wife and queen of the elected King Claudius Conomorus, has ruled ably in her own right since the disappearance of King Claudius some ten years ago. Known for her generous support of local charitable institutions, sponsorship of the arts, and infrastructure projects, Queen Millona used the power of her throne in the service of the common people, a trait altogether too rare in these times.

The Abecean Monitor makes no secret of its longstanding support for the deposed Queen Millona. While our staff are disappointed in this outcome, we ask that the new Queen consider with fresh eyes the many wise decisions of her good-hearted predecessor, and continue to support this newspaper's editorial independence. The Monitor is a critical paper of record for the entire Abecean region, one which informs readers from Taneth to Firsthold on the happenings that most affect their lives. We look forward to a new and productive journalistic relationship with Queen Akaterina and her administration.

A contemporary of Tiber Septim himself, she once ruled Morrowind as its first Queen following the Armistice, and helped put an end to the Imperial Simulacrum. While her son is now our King, rumor has it that the crown was offered to her first. Is the Queen Mother the real power behind the throne? Read all about it on page six.

LONG-STANDING WAR TAX REPEALED

In a generous decree, Emperor Uriel Septim VII, long may be his reign, surprised the Empire by repealing the venerable war tax. Set to enter its 34th year, the tax was established to aid in recovery after the disastrous Simulacrum. Phrere Briricca, director of the Old Ebonheart branch of the Briricca Private Bank, comments that the repeal marks the restoration of normalcy: "The more prosperous citizens have long suffered under an outsized tax burden. Now, wealth can flow freer than ever. I see nothing but prosperity ahead for our Empire."

A NEW CITIZEN CONTRIBUTION

In the same decree, the Emperor revealed a new household tax, "not exceeding 10 Septims," to be used for road maintenance. Responding to criticism that the new tax simply shifts the burden from the rich to the masses, Phrere Briricca explained: "Disregard that nonsense. There is nothing more fair than a flat, per-household tax. Any responsible family should be able to cover the cost handily." Readers owning property worth more than 30000 Septims will be pleased to hear that their total tax burden will, indeed, be decreasing as a result of these changes.

HELSETH HOSTS ARGONIAN EMISSARY

Following rising tensions in the Arnesian border regions, High King Hlaalu Helseth hosted the Argonian emissary to Morrowind, Im-Kilaya, at a state banquet at the Royal Palace of Mournhold. A spokesperson for the King told reporters the pair discussed the situation along the Morrowind - Black Marsh border, and the King expressed his regret that House Dres declined to send their own representatives to participate in the discussion. The Arnesian jungle remains a hotbed for conflict, as Argonian irregulars continue to raid Dark Elf caravans. It seems unlikely that the cycle of violence will die down any time soon, as resentment about territory lost some thirty years ago still festers among the local Argonian tribes, and the Dark Elves continue to uphold the barbaric practice of slavery.

TEXT.old:
OUR CITY'S TAVERNS REVIEWED

New to our fair city? Looking for a place to forget the troubles of the road? Fret not, the Bellman has you covered! Our correspondents have visited, rated, and ranked all our taverns, inns and boarding houses, for your convenience.

The Moth and Tiger
Despite its unassuming exterior, this establishment offers the finest lodgings and drinks in all of Ebonheart. Do try its impressive selection of wines. Travelers longing for the comforts of home need look no further than the first building to the right as they enter our city through the main gate. Not to be confused with the Legion Boarding House across the street, which only serves Legion recruits, poorly.

The Mother Alessia
Our city's best bakery is located at the intersection just past the Moth and Tiger. While it offers no lodgings or drinks, it makes up for this with the quality of its baked goods. The Mother Alessia is well-renowned for its biscuits, specialty bread, and pies. Indeed, it is said that the unsurpassed quality of the Mother Alessia is the reason why so many bakers find their way to our city, eager to sample its wares and glean its recipes.

The Empress Katariah
The oldest of our city's taverns, this establishment's beds are acceptable, its food serviceable, and its drinks cheap. While the building has seen better days, it is worth a visit for its colourful clientele. Strike up a conversation with its regulars, and you are bound to have an interesting time. Its bartender, on the other hand, is far less talkative, which ensures that patrons' secrets will not be spilled by the serving staff.

Hostel of Stendarr's Mercy
While those new to our city might be misled by the name, the Hostel of Stendarr's Mercy does not serve common travelers. Instead it is dedicated to the rehabilitation of those citizens unfortunate enough to have found themselves enslaved by the Dark Elves. Those of means and generous spirit may nevertheless wish to visit the hostel on Craftsmen Street to leave a donation and allow the good work to continue.

The Salty Futtocks
Located on the eastern side of the city, this establishment has little to offer to well-off travelers. Worse, it is notorious for its watered-down liquor and frequent bar brawls. Adventurous travelers looking for a good time might feel tempted to pay the place a visit, but be warned: you are just as likely to find a knife to the back, instead. Surely the guards would have shut the tavern down long ago, were it not for the diversion it offers the dregs of society.

Six Fishes
Should you find yourself in Ebonheart-on-Vvardenfell, the Six Fishes offers rooms and interesting drinking companions to any traveler. While the inn is not particularly exceptional, its visitors are varied and have many a tale to tell about the hazards of the island. For the adventurous traveler, a visit should prove instructional, but those that prefer more refined comforts would do well to stay on the mainland.

EBONY EXPORTS STRENGTHEN TROOPS

The Caldera Mining Company continues to export vast quantities of ebony to the Imperial Province. Now, the great benefits of our access to this precious material are becoming evident to all, as a splendid set of armor made of Caldera ebony was delivered to our city all the way from the Legion's master armorers in the Imperial Heartland. Made specifically for Lord General Caecalia Victrix, the deep-black armor is studded with ruby and inlaid with golden dragons. Such richly decorated armor is rightfully reserved for the higher ranks of our Legions. Our brave soldiers need not fret, however, as the staff of the Grand Marshal is considering enhancing our troops' uniforms with specific ebony reinforcements. Caldera ebony is set to save the lives of many!

BELLMAN INVESTMENT TIPS
BY MASTER TRADER JOLUS HERDANE

Hoom milk! It's the hottest new investment opportunity, straight from the frigid Velothis! Now, boo-booers out there might be thinking that my latest tip, dreugh whistles, received a minor safety warning from the Imperial Commission, while the one before that, the Imperial Velk Nectar Company, ran into slight legal issues with the Dark Elves. But hoom milk is one rock solid opportunity! In fact, I've got a shipload of the stuff on a multi-month journey to Elsweyr already - the cat-folk will lap it up in no time! You'd be dumb not to invest!

CALDERA MINE SHUTS DOWN

Grave news recently arrived from Vvardenfell: The Caldera Mine, the largest Imperial ebony mining operation on the island, has shut down! It is as of yet unclear what has caused the mining operations to cease, but speculations range from a slave uprising to a coordinated, wholesale slaughter of the mine administration by an agent of House Redoran. From our diligent reporting, though, one thing has become clear: should the shut-down not be resolved quickly, this event could turn out to be disastrous. The town of Caldera is economically dependent on the mines, and any lasting disruption would see Imperial citizens lose work and be forced to resettle in droves. Thankfully, this crisis in the West Gash has not, and likely will not, affected the economical prospects of Old Ebonheart. The Bellman would therefore remind all citizens that the Imperial Cult is always collecting alms for the poor, and any donations made in these trying times by those of us not affected by monetary hardships would be a welcome relief for those in need.

TEXT.old:
TOURNAMENT DELAYED AGAIN!

Aspiring champions assembled for the highly anticipated Ebon Hill Tournament have expressed their disappointment and indignation following Castellan Caros Cocceius' announcement that proceedings are to be placed on indefinite hold once again, leaving competitors languishing!

The tournament, celebrating the rule of His Majesty, King Hlaalu Helseth was expected to go ahead soon, with grand tents already erected in preparation outside the Ebonheart city walls, but has been plagued with delays. Absent representatives, missing equipment, and disputes over everything from refreshment vendors to the rumored grand prize have dampened enthusiasm among some city residents and aspirants alike.

One guild representative who wishes to remain anonymous told the Bellman, "It's no major concern for those of us who reside in the city, but some competitors and their entourages have traveled from much farther afield and have been left twiddling their thumbs in tents, or renting accommodation for far longer than planned. I worry they are being left at a disadvantage."

Others argue that the lingering retinues have been a boon for local businesses.

Representatives from organizations across Morrowind, from Imperial Guilds to Dark Elf Houses, and the royal court itself are expected to compete in a melee in the High Rock style... Just as soon as the Castellan gives the word!

TEXT.old:
COURT WIZARD PASSES AWAY

Castellan Caros Cocceius has confirmed the passing of Talis Nerethril, Ebonheart's court wizard. A popular figure within the Ebon Tower, Wizard Nerethril's tenure was marked by a commitment to research, especially in the field of extraplanar teleology. He was also highly respected for his diligent mentorship of his two apprentices, Kelkemmello and Saturius.

Nerethril's death will undoubtedly come as a shock to many citizens. The castellan has announced his intention to name a new court wizard "with all haste", but it is unclear how he'll go about the selection process; the Bellman understands that Nerethril left no record of whom he wished to succeed him.

Wizard Nerethril is survived by his son, Methal, who requests privacy in this difficult time.

TEXT.old:
A NEW COURT WIZARD

Following a period of vacancy for the position, Ebonheart's new court wizard has been named at last: the High Elf Kelkemmello, one of two apprentices kept by the previous court wizard, Talis Nerethril.

While Ebonheart's court wizards have traditionally picked their successors directly, Wizard Nerethril's tragic and untimely death made this impossible. The ideal candidate was instead selected through a series of three challenges designed to test their participants' magical prowess. Kelkemmello claims that emerging victorious was no tall order.

"My performance in the challenges distinguished me as the obvious choice for Ebonheart's court wizard," he told the Bellman after his triumph. "I look forward to taking my rightful position."

As the Bellman celebrates Wizard Kelkemmello's new title, it would also like to pay its respects to Wizard Nerethril one more time. May he find peace with his ancestors.

TEXT.old:
SEDITIOUS LICH THWARTED

Each and every one of Ebonheart's citizens may sleep a little more soundly tonight. Sharnoga gra-Mal, steward of the Fighters Guild's Ebonheart branch, recently announced the vanquishing of a centuries-old lich with a grudge against our city. A contemporary of Tiber Septim, Galmyne Dobar became well-known for her hit and run attacks against Imperials following the signing of the Armistice. After years of this merciless slaughter, a Fighters Guild contract led to Dobar's seeming defeat. No further incidents involving her had been reported until now.

The Bellman is assured that this time, she will stay down! The fearless %PCClass, %PCName, is said to have banished the lich's very soul, eliminating any possibility of her returning again. The achievement was recognized with a reward from Queen Barenziah herself. It looks like we can chalk up one more victory for Tiber Septim!

OTREBUS DELAGIA FOUND DEAD

Otrebus Delagia, a local businessman, has been found dead, sources say. Delagia, a Cyrodiil native, was allegedly the head of a criminal enterprise known as "Delagia's gang". The news of his death has reportedly come as a relief to some living on the east side of town. Whether or not Delagia's death was a natural one has not been confirmed. The townsguard declined to comment.

DAEDRIC THREATS ON THE DECLINE

Extraplanar threats to the Empire have reached an all time low, according to a recent study coming from the Imperial City. Scholars and mages in service of the Empire have closely monitored the realms of Oblivion and discovered that hostile Daedric endeavors have all but ceased completely. "The waters of Oblivion are silent", the scholars assure us. May we enjoy these peaceful times as long as they may last.

TEXT.old:
COLONY ESTABLISHED ON SOLSTHEIM

The East Empire Company, always intent on providing the people of the Empire with new opportunities for wealth and prosperity, has established a new settlement on the island of Solstheim. Situated far north in the Sea of Ghosts, the island provides a welcome change from Morrowind's otherwise brown and dusty environments, with beautiful shorelines, green trees, glistening snow and fresh air. The settlement itself, a booming little town called Raven Rock, is a wellspring of opportunity just waiting for people to take advantage of. Whether it is driving ebony out of the ground, building sturdy homes from plentiful lumber, or simply serving the local brews at the bar, work there is rewarding and well-paid. Truly a place to call home. If you are interested in helping the EEC bring their venture to fruition, apply at the East Empire Company office today!

TEXT.old:
NECROMANCY BANNED IN OUR CITY

In a surprise announcement, Imperial Magistrate Belisatha Mede decreed that necromancy shall henceforth be banned in the city of Old Ebonheart. The Magistrate justified the decision as necessary in order to further peaceful and profitable relations with the natives, who abhor the practice.

Some have criticised the decree, arguing that Imperial Law should apply uniformly across the Empire without allowances for local customs. An unnamed representative of the native Temple was seen visiting several Old Ebonheart notables in days prior, raising concerns that the organization is being granted too much influence over provincial affairs.

Certified necromancer Hastophos Velifer is furious: "With one stroke, the Magistrate and the Tribunal Temple have taken away my livelihood. Did you know that the Dunmer themselves practice necromancy? Their own tombs are brimming with reanimated guardians, but to us they forbid even saying goodbye to passed relatives!"

However, others are optimistic that the Dark Elves will respond in kind to this act of goodwill, perhaps regarding statutes that allow the practice of slavery to persist.

Sjoring's brother Radd, a high-ranking and respected member of the Imperial Legion, had this to say: "I don't know. Sjoring was one of the best damn fighters I knew. TEXT.old:
ARCH-MAGE KILLED IN DUEL

Dramatic events are underway in the Vvardenfell Mages Guild. Arch-Mage Trebonius Artorius, a famous battlemage in his own right, was reportedly struck down in a duel against a fellow Guild mage. Circumstances around the duel are murky -- rumors suggest essentially a mutiny within the guild, with Artorius standing accused of ineffectual leadership. The Bellman's local Mages Guild contacts, themselves not under the jurisdiction of the Vvardenfell hierarchy, vehemently denied the possibility of any conspiracy within the Mages Guild. However, one source added ominously: "No one is surprised at what happened to Trebonius." It is, as of yet, unclear whether the guild's supreme council is aware of the developments, nor what their response will be. We can only hope for no interruptions in the essential services the Mages Guild provides in the untamed Vvardenfell frontier.

THIEVES GUILD DECAPITATED!

Today, the Bellman has some exclusive, shocking news for you! After careful investigation, our reporters have discovered an alarming pattern in a recent string of killings in popular Vvardenfell hangouts: all of the victims were ranking members of the Thieves Guild! While local authorities have not yet apprehended a suspect, our analysts suspect that the murders were a coordinated assault on the Guild by its longstanding rivals, the Camonna Tong. Nominally a society of "businessmer" championing Dark Elf interests, Camonna operatives smuggle chartered goods and slaves by the boatful, and casually murder anyone who might pose a threat to their criminal enterprise. With the comparatively restrained and principled Thieves' Guild decapitated, a dark cloud descends over the Imperial province of Morrowind as the Camonna Tong's brutality lowers the standards of decency even among criminals.

VVARDENFELL CRIME RISING

According to an Imperial Legion source, trouble is brewing on the island of Vvardenfell, with smuggling, thievery, and even killings on the rise. Coast Guard patrols are apprehending an increasing number of smugglers in the Bitter Coast region, while rumors speak of turf wars between rival street gangs in Balmora. Most disturbing is a wave of murders, seemingly targeting innocent citizens -- up to five Imperial settlers have been brutally killed in the past weeks in Vivec City alone. It is difficult to assess the root cause of all these disturbances, but fanatical Dark Elf separatists are a prime suspect. This is a sobering development for many in Old Ebonheart, who have profited handsomely from Vvardenfell settlement.

TEXT.old:
CRAZY CULTIST CAUSES COMMOTION

Recently, there has been some uproar amongst the members of the native Tribunal Temple about something called a "Nerevarine". Apparently, an insane adventurer who only recently arrived in Morrowind is now claiming to fulfill a sacrilegious prophecy. This has caused a great stir among Temple devotees, with many priests calling for the outlander's immediate arrest and execution. The situation leaves this humble reporter wondering: if it is forbidden to fulfill, why have a prophecy in the first place? In any case, Ebon Tower officials have assured us that this is not the first case of such a "prophecy claimant". Taking this into account, the situation is sure to calm down and things should return to normal in a manner of weeks, at most.
