HOUSE ELVES ELECT HORTATOR

Following a period of religious unrest and political jockeying among the native factions, the Temple of the Dark Elves declared that an immigrant %PCRace has been elected Hortator of the Grand Council. Hortator is apparently not just the name of a popular card game, but also an ancient honorific bestowed upon the war chief of the Dark Elf armies. Why the notoriously xenophobic natives chose to confer this title upon a foreigner remains unclear. Informed sources tell us that the office of the Hortator has stood empty for at least two decades.

BELLMAN ANALYSIS:
UPRISING IMMINENT?

Does this Hortator pose a threat to Imperial hegemony? Citizens worried about potential Dark Elf uprisings can rest assured, so says one of the Bellman's anonymous Legion contacts: "The terms of the Armistice forbid the natives from maintaining a standing army, leaving this war chief without warriors to command. This whole affair sounds like internal Dark Elf politics to me. Besides, what can a single %PCRace possibly hope to achieve?"

Citizens worried about potential Dark Elf uprisings can rest assured, so says one of the Bellman's anonymous Legion contacts: "The terms of the Armistice forbid the natives from maintaining a standing army, leaving this war chief without warriors to command. This whole affair sounds like internal Dark Elf politics to me. Besides, what can a single %PCRace possibly hope to achieve?"

TEXT.old:
DAGOTH UR DEFEATED

Dagoth Ur, the immortal enemy of the Dark Elven people and the source of the corruption at the heart of Vvardenfell, has been vanquished. This feat is attributed to the heroic %PCRace %PCName, an agent of our Emperor, who strode into Red Mountain and did battle with the ancient devil and his host of malformed monsters. Details of the events that transpired beneath Red Mountain are scarce, but it is clear that our Empire has won a great victory against the forces that seek to destabilize it.

Though little was known about the exact nature of the devil Dagoth Ur, it was well established that the Red Mountain region was home to an insidious and expanding threat to the Imperial province of Morrowind. Conflicting sources characterized Dagoth Ur as either an exceptionally powerful sorcerer, a malevolent spirit, a fallen demigod, or a metaphor for the depravity of man and mer. Whatever the case may be, the entity appears to have been at the center of a dangerous cult of Dark Elf separatists. Normally tight-lipped sources in the upper echelons of the Imperial administration confirmed that the Emperor himself had taken a keen interest in the threat posed by Dagoth Ur and his worshippers. Their defeat proves once more that nothing can withstand the might of the Emperor, long may he reign!

VVARDENFELL BLIGHT STORMS RECEDE

Scouts report that along with the fall of Dagoth Ur, blight storms have entirely receded from Red Mountain. The sickening mystical ash storms once engulfed the region with no interruption, but skies are now clear around central Vvardenfell for the first time in Imperial memory. This calls for quick action in securing Imperial land grants: the untapped resources of Red Mountain could enrich the Empire in Morrowind for generations to come.

TEXT.old:
KING MOVES TO CONSOLIDATE POWER

King Helseth, the rightful monarch of the province of Morrowind, has unveiled a bold new initiative to overhaul the governance of the province. The Armistice, which established the Empire's hold on Morrowind, essentially left the day-to-day governance of large parts of the province to Dark Elf Great Houses. However, King Helseth points to recent attacks by strange beasts and magical weather disasters in the native capital, which the Great Houses seemed unable to prevent, and calls for a stronger central authority. In this challenge, the King is backed by what he says is the personal support of the Dark Elf goddess Almalexia. The Temple has protested this interpretation of the goddess' will, but there is room for doubt, unless Almalexia herself were to confirm her position.

TEXT.old:
HLAALU HALT PROMISING PROPERTY

An ambitious Dark Elven construction project on the northern shores of Lake Andaram has been placed on indefinite hold amidst heated disputes between feuding Great Houses, leaving some Imperial investors high and dry.

The new settlement, Nav Andaram, had previously been approved by His Majesty King Hlaalu Helseth and was slated to feature a wealth of retail properties, shipping facilities, and even a purpose-built Chapel of Talos in an under-served region of the province.

House Indoril assert that the project, spearheaded by the industrious House Hlaalu, was a "deliberate provocation" against their House, and that eastern banks of the Thirr are the "exclusive and ancestral domain of House Indoril". We think the great city of Ebonheart might have something to say about that!

TEXT.old:
IMPERIAL TREASURES STOLEN!

Is the Empire in Morrowind under a coordinated, covert attack? This seems to be the implication of a series of recent break-ins to Imperial institutions in both Old Ebonheart and Ebonheart-on-Vvardenfell. While guards reportedly managed to fend off a burglary in the Ebon Tower vaults, brigands stole a precious ancient cuirass and sword in the care of the Imperial Legion on Vvardenfell. What's worse, the offenders are rumored to have been traitors from within the Legion itself. If outside enemies are now combining forces with treasonous elements in the Imperial ranks, this surely heralds dangerous times for the Empire in the East.

However, when asked to comment, Lord General Caecalia Victrix of the Morrowind Imperial Legion denied that citizens should be concerned: "There is no need for undue alarm. We have no evidence that the attacks were in any way connected. Rest assured, these are simple thieves, who will quickly be apprehended and the treasures will soon be returned to the rightful possession of the Emperor Uriel Septim VII, long may be his reign." We can only wish good fortune to the Imperial Legion as it seeks to recover the lost artifacts.

TEXT.old:
KNIGHTS RECOVER LOST ARTIFACTS

The Imperial Legion reports coming back into possession of priceless treasures shamelessly stolen from the Imperial Commission in Ebonheart-on-Vvardenfell. The Lord's Mail, a legendary cuirass long guarded by the Imperial Legion, was taken by a disgraced former legionary who abused his knowledge of the castle to betray his once-comrades. The thief resisted arrest and had to be put down by Imperial Legion knights. Chrysamere, also known as the Paladin's Blade, was taken by another traitorous knight and had since come into the possession of the illegal sorceress Draramu Hloran. The sorceress reportedly used the blade to terrorize the inhabitants of Sadrith Mora, who presumably feel great relief at the apprehension of the outlaw.

Lord General Caecalia Victrix of the Imperial Legion in Morrowind is jubilant: "With these decisive strikes, the Knights of the Imperial Legion demonstrated the cunning and ruthlessness that all traitors to the Imperial cause will have to reckon with. The Legion has once again reaffirmed the might of the Emperor Uriel Septim VII, long may he reign!" Glory to the Emperor!

TEXT.old:
EBONHEART FASHION TRENDSETTER

Aetia Nemesia, the formidable top administrator of the East Empire Company, may also be the most fashionable woman in the city. Recently, she wowed the city's elite society with her sleek new outfit of tight-fitting cream trousers, a deep-blue velvet robe tastefully ornamented with golden embroidery and matching silken shoes, tailor-made to suit the fast-paced lifestyle of the foremost merchant in Old Ebonheart. Note that all of Aetia's garments are ordered straight from the finest couturier houses in Cyrodiil City, representing the latest in Imperial design. In her own words, "Life is too short for half measures. I dress the same way I run my EEC chapter: ruthlessly, without false scruples." Whether shocked or thrilled by these new winds in fashion, one thing is clear: in matters of style, this is a woman to keep in mind.

TEXT.old:
GRIFT EXPOSED IN EEC

The East Empire Company in Old Ebonheart was shocked to discover it's former top administrator, Aetia Nemesia, has for several years been skimming from company coffers and collaborating with criminal elements. The disgraced official is currently on route to a trial in Cyrodiil City. Behind the investigation was Merxia Vendicci, head of one of the prime families in Old Ebonheart and Director of the EEC. "I want to stress that this outrage was the singular work of a corrupt official. In uncovering this crime, I was able to rely on the overall incorruptible and loyal nature of most EEC employees," she maintains. Despite Vendicci's assurances, charges such as these have long dogged the EEC, who maintain substantial operations in remote Imperial outposts, often beyond the immediate grasp of its central administration.

BELLMAN ANALYSIS:
STYLE ISN'T EVERYTHING

The editorial team would like to express dismay at the outrageous corruption displayed by Aetia Nemesia, until recently considered by many to be an exemplary member of the city's elite. This goes to show something the Bellman has always stressed: don't be fooled by good appearances. In fact, many in the team have always been suspicious of Nemesia's extravagant manners.

TEXT.old:
MAGES GUILD MONOPOLY GONE

The Grand Council of Vvardenfell has introduced specific exemptions to the Guilds Act within the district. The resolution was proposed by the Telvanni representative and pushed through by a united front of the island's dominant Dark Elf Houses. It appears that the native factions temporarily set aside their differences for the purpose of hurting Imperial interests and labor protections. Though the wording of the resolution targets a wide array of arts and crafts, the move appears to be the latest assault on the Guild of Mages by the sorcerous House Telvanni. Sources within the Mages Guild decry the resolution, fearful that the new exemptions will flood the magical market with dangerous enchantments and encourage charlatans to pose as legitimate instructors.

BELLMAN ANALYSIS:
EXPECT DRAWN-OUT LEGAL CHALLENGES

The Guild of Mages is sure to challenge the legality of the new resolution. The Guilds Act of the Second Era leaves little ambiguity as far as the primacy of the Imperial Guilds is concerned, though the Armistice affords the district councils a large amount of leeway to introduce their own local rules and regulations regarding commerce. While the Bellman does not doubt that Imperial interests will ultimately prevail, the real question is whether House Telvanni will accept a ruling, or simply ignore the courts.

TEXT.old:
RED SECUNDA STUMPS ASTROLOGERS

A spectacular sight occurred in the skies above our city as Secunda suddenly and without warning turned a deep crimson color. The unexplained discoloration lasted a number of days before the small moon reverted to its regular appearance, as though nothing at all had happened. The scholarly community is working overtime to study the cause and the implications of this event, but so far, no one satisfying explanation for the phenomenon has been proposed. Hypotheses range from high-altitude ash clouds to dark magics. Meanwhile, the Imperial Astrological Society is reportedly in disarray, having its long-held beliefs of Secunda as a stabilizing agent in our omens roundly shattered. Its members now fervently debate whether the crimson color indicates that the red ruby of our Empire will reign supreme, or whether a tide of blood will wash us all away. Unless the phenomenon repeats itself and the Imperial Mananauts stand at the ready to take a closer look, a satisfying answer may never be found.

KHAJIIT SURVIVES TALOS' TOWER TUMBLE

During this strange celestial phenomenon, a small group of Khajiit diplomats from the Elsweyr mission scrambled to the top of Talos' Tower and, in an apparent fit of moon-madness, started performing what seemed to be an acrobatics routine. Alas, as the diplomats stood balancing on one another's shoulders, a stiff breeze blew the top cat off of the tower and sent her tumbling down into the courtyard below. Miraculously, she was found completely unscathed, though clearly greatly confused, as she clamored: "Oh Jone! We are too few and too feeble to brave Khenarthi's breath! Who now will pry the Lattice from the Hungry Cat's claws?"

TEXT.old:
ARTS AND CULTURE EDITION

This week, the Bellman staff are proud to feature book reviews by Conjur, an employee of the Zafirbel Bay Company in Helnim.

"The Arrowshot Woman", various authors

This collection of tall tales and fables from exotic Elsweyr will delight citizens from all walks of life. A weighty tome, filled with adventure. Recommended for young readers!

"The Necklace", Ormax Endre

The Empire's mandate to rule Tamriel rests not only on legions and levies, but also the heavenly stream of artistic inspiration that flows from the Nine Divines into man and mer. With fast-paced prose and deadly stakes, this pulse-pounding novel soars ever-towards its shocking twist ending. No, this novel is not for the faint of heart. In short, meddle not in the affairs of dragons, dear reader!

"The Hope of the Redoran", Turiul Nirith

This provincial classic is an ideal introduction to the ancient culture of Morrowind's native Great Houses. Great House Redoran venerates honor, loyalty, and solemnity, principles the reader will encounter in spades. This Dunmer morality tale on pride and trial by combat comes highly recommended.

TEXT.old:
LICH LAID LOW

The Knights of the Order of Ebonheart report that the undead menace infesting the Saros Archipelago is no more. Imperial forces are expected to secure the area in the coming weeks.

Years ago, a skeletal horde headed by the lich Grurn overran the Imperial fortifications on the archipelago, creating a danger to shipping in that section of the Inner Sea. The Order of Ebonheart was tasked with assembling a strike force to infiltrate the ruined Fort Firemoth and vanquish its unlawful occupant. Thanks to the hard work of these loyal citizens, the source of the threat has been removed and the dragon banner will once more fly above the battlements.

TEXT.old:
INNER SEA SECURED

The proud banners of the Empire grace the walls of Fort Firemoth and Sulphurwatch Keep once more. After vanquishing the undead horde occupying the archipelago, the Imperial Legion and Imperial Navy joined hands to rebuild these fortifications raised to guard the Inner Sea. The future looked bleak for a moment when the Vvardenfell District Grand Council sought to dispute direct Imperial control, but thankfully Duke Dren was able to dismiss the matter after the intervention of a skilled Legion negotiator.

Through the generous donations and hard work of loyal citizens, both Fort Firemoth and Sulphurwatch Keep are operational once again. Commodore Kventus Lucilius has already moved his detachment out of Fort Ancylis and back to its traditional home of Sulphurwatch Keep. Meanwhile, Lord General Caecalia Victrix has appointed %PCName as commandant of Fort Firemoth. This %PCRace played a vital role in liberating the archipelago from Grurn and assisted in the rebuilding of the fort.

TEXT.old:
CRIMINAL SYNDICATE RESPONSIBLE FOR DRUG CRISIS

Narsis City Watch has confirmed that an emerging criminal power, known as the Ja-Natta Syndicate, is responsible for the epidemic of a drug known as "greydust" which has swept through the poorer quarters of Narsis like an ash-storm.

While skooma-related crimes and deaths remain at an all-too-high yet consistent level, Narsis citizens have increasingly reported dangerous greydust addicts in the streets. Symptoms of greydust usage include erratic and violent behavior, lack of appetite leading to dangerous weight loss, and a pale grey pallor to the skin of users who are nearing death.

According to a statement to The Canyon Echo by Deputy Captain of the Watch Andres Hlaalo, the Ja-Natta Syndicate is the sole producer of greydust. While Temple alchemists have attempted to identify the formula for the dangerous drug, they have not yet been successful, according to Diviner Farona Darvel. This suggests that members of the Ja-Natta Syndicate are skilled alchemists. Representatives of the Guild of Mages have declined to comment.

Syndicate members are also reported to be organized and violent. If Narsis citizens witness mixed-race groups who are lightly armored and wielding blunt weapons, or carrying no weapons at at all, moving through the streets or outlying country with purpose, they are advised not to attempt to confront the group. Official advice from the City Watch is to report such activity to your nearest Hlaalu Guard.

Long-time readers may recall The Canyon Echo's article on the 4th of Rain's Hand reporting on the growing numbers of controlled enchanted weapons, such as spark-, jink-, and viperblades, moving through Morrowind's smuggling networks. Further investigation has revealed that this activity may also be connected to the Ja-Natta Syndicate, who are known for their use of enchanted weapons.

Violent turf wars in Narsis' sewers may also be tied to a Syndicate presence. "I'm scared to do my job," said a maintenance worker, who wished to remain anonymous for fear of reprisal. "Every day there's a fresh bloodstain on the tiles, or a body floating in the water. You hear screams echoing through the tunnels. It's like a battlefield down there." Until recently, gang activity in the sewers has been kept under control by the Camonna Tong. If the Syndicate is challenging the Tong for control of the sewers, this may lead to an explosion of independent criminal activity.

Citizens of Narsis must hope that the City Watch can bring the Ja-Natta Syndicate under control, and arrest its unknown leadership, before the violence erupts onto Narsis streets. "We are co-operating with the Imperial Legion to track down the leadership of the Ja-Natta Syndicate," said Andres Hlaalo, "They have been diligent in fighting the Syndicate since it emerged in Tear, but so far have been unable to locate the powers behind the organization." While Hlaalo declined to comment on House Redoran in his statement, he confirmed that the City Watch were investigating sources of Syndicate activity downriver. The Canyon Echo has reached out to Felmaru Llendu, House Redoran governor of Ald Iuval, for comment, but the Echo has received no reply.

BLACK MARSH TRADE DWINDLES AMIDST REBELLION

The Census & Excise Office at Stormgate Pass has reported a 40% reduction in traffic passing through the border post in the last quarter of 3E426. This comes as fears in this city, and throughout the southern border region, grow that the Soulrest rebellion may spread even further throughout Black Marsh. The savage natives, who took control of the southwestern part of the province last year, have plunged the wider area into anarchy. Many traders in Narsis still have grim memories of the Arnesian War and the Argonian barbarism that claimed the lives of many innocent people less than thirty years ago. The decline of trade between Narsis and our sister city Stormhold has resulted in several Narsis businesses struggling to remain open. Sources within the Temple indicate that the amount of mer relying on donations for the poor has risen sharply over the past year.

TEXT.old:
FOREIGN QUARTER KILLER BROUGHT TO JUSTICE

Hlalur Galan, a former butcher known to many as the Foreign Quarter Killer, has been arrested by the Canyon Watch. This infamous murderer killed eight Imperial women in Narsis over the past months, and his capture has reassured many of our Cyrodiilic citizens of the Watch's efficiency at punishing such crimes. "I knew a few friends who had been found dead in their beds," recounted Musa Talania to a Canyon Echo reporter. "At a certain point, I had to start sleeping with a dagger just to feel safe. I'm so glad that the Watch has finally put this criminal where he belongs." According to Deputy Captain of the Canyon Watch Andres Hlaalo, the murders may have been Galan's attempt to attract the Camonna Tong's attention in an effort to join the gang. Due to the nature of his crimes, he has been sentenced to fight in the Narsis Arena until his death.

The Echo sends its condolences to any relatives or friends of the killer's victims, and hopes that they may find comfort in his just fate.

STORMY SEAS SINK SHIP OFF VVARDENFELL

Stormy conditions in Azura's Coast have wrecked the ship "Prelude" off southern Vvardenfell, and several crew members are believed to have drowned. The ship's owner, Dravos Turil, has confirmed that it carried valuable cargo, but refused to disclose any specifics to Echo reporters. Any ships traveling through the coast should be cautious of sailing in rough weather.

EEC CRUSHES MINERS' REVOLT

Sapphire miners in Num-Ittu Mine were recently coerced into ending a rebellion originally started for better wages. The mine, owned and operated by the East Empire Company, was a major source of income for it, but the workers never saw much of the profits themselves. According to a Company official who chose to remain anonymous, a mercenary known as %PCName was hired from the Fighters Guild to put down the revolt -- by any means necessary. Confirmed reports have been received that multiple miners were killed, possibly in an effort to scare any remaining back to work. The Echo wishes to remind the EEC that it bears responsibility for the safety of its employees, and denounces the cruel actions it has taken.

EEC DEFEATS MINERS' REVOLT

Sapphire miners in Num-Ittu Mine were recently coerced into ending a rebellion originally started for better wages. The mine, owned and operated by the East Empire Company, was a major source of income for it, but workers have reported that almost none of the profits ever went to them. According to the foreman of the mine, Linia Trellus, the Company sent in a mercenary known as %PCName from the Fighters Guild to put down the revolt -- by any means necessary: "I got roughed up pretty bad. Not sure I'll be able to hold a pick right for at least a few months. I've thanked the Divines there wasn't any more bloodshed, but I never thought the Company would do something like this." Rogatus Cipius, the Factor of the EEC's Narsis branch, did not respond to the Echo's request for comment.

NUM-ITTU STANDOFF ENDS

Sapphire miners in Num-Ittu Mine recently agreed to end a rebellion originally started for better wages. The mine, owned and operated by the East Empire Company, was a major source of income for it, but the workers never saw much of the profits themselves. According to the foreman of the mine, Linia Trellus, the Company sent in a mercenary known as %PCName from the Fighters Guild to put down the revolt: "I thought they were coming to scare us into backing off, but I guess even sellswords know how to bargain sometimes." Rogatus Cipius, the Factor of the EEC's Narsis branch, had this to say: "The Company cares about its workers' requests. We are negotiators first and foremost, and are careful to seek out peaceful solutions where possible."

RIGGED FIGHTS IN THE NARSIS ARENA?

Suspicious activity surrounding one of the Narsis Arena's recent fights has cast doubt on the institution's integrity. After longtime combatant Ralvam Turil lost a round against the rising star %PCName, Dravos Turil, one of the Arena's biggest investors and father to Ralvam, withdrew all his former monetary support. Additionally, the victorious %PCRace was banned from any further fights, with no declared cause. Echo reporters, in an attempt to shed light on the situation, have gleaned some surprising information from an anonymous source in the Arena. Not only was %PCName offered a bribe to lose a match, but many other competitors going up against Ralvam were also offered bribes -- all supposedly by Dravos Turil. Such news raises troubling questions: Could other fights have been rigged? What does this mean for the betting markets? Whatever the answers would be, trust in the Arena has been shaken, and it may take some time to be regained.

MASSACRE IN BALMORA SYMPTOM OF LARGER CRIME SPREE

While the recent murder of several innocent citizens at Balmora's Council Club may seem like an isolated, if tragic, incident, some disturbing signs have pointed to a more sinister motivation behind the act. A number of similar attacks have taken place recently, all perpetrated against other businesses, by the Thieves' Guild. It seems that since the opening of Vvardenfell and with its continued colonization, the organization has been emboldened to commit these acts of sabotage and violence, which will only escalate further if not dealt with swiftly. But the Empire's justice is often slow to move -- why, the Guild is practically considered a legitimate enterprise in some parts of Cyrodiil! And if the law continues to stand idly by while such events take place unhindered, then it can be easily understood why some might decide to take matters into their own hands, lest this pattern claims their lives as well.

INVESTMENT SPOTLIGHTS

In Telvannis District to the far northeast, the small trade town of Helnim hides plenty of profit to be made with a stake in its most prominent enterprise: the Zafirbel Bay Company. While not yet as widely known as its friendly competitor, the East Empire Company, the ZBC has already established a firm trading partnership with the nearby Telvanni settlement of Tel Gilan. They sell kwama eggs, bug musk, and saltrice at reasonable prices, and are sure to provide a sizable return on any investments you make.

VEHK SPEAKS! PERSECUTION OF NEREVARINE TO END

In a shocking turn of events, the %PCRace proclaiming themselves to be Nerevarine was granted an audience with Vivec, and officially recognized by the Temple as Saint Nerevar reborn. This declaration, the first such public announcement by any of the Three in decades, has surprised many of Almsivi's faithful. On inquiry, a Temple representative said, "I never would have thought that an outlander could be granted such an honor, but if Lord Vivec wills it, then it must be so." In addition to the end of the Nerevarine's persecution by the Temple, the previously illegal sect known as the Dissident Priests will no longer be branded as heretics, and allowed to rejoin their brethren. While it remains to be seen what effects this decision will have in the long run, such a shift in Temple doctrine is sure to herald substantial change.

BANDIT ACTIVITY NEAR BORDERS INCREASES

Outlaws have attacked and robbed multiple caravans on the roads south of Narsis in the past months. While the Canyon Watch has ensured that there has been no bloodshed near the city itself, the high Shipal canyons can hide thugs and robbers much more easily. Merchants with goods traveling through Stormgate Pass should be wary of suspicious activity in the area, and make sure to hire armed guards from reputable organizations.

IN MEMORIAM: ORVAS DREN

Orvas Dren has been recently found dead in his home, murdered by an unknown assailant. The son of Releniah Dren and brother of Duke Vedam Dren, Orvas played an integral part in supporting the Dunmer community's interests in Narsis. Under his patronage, local businesses were protected from opportunistic western monopolies, and many among us recall his passionate speeches that gave even the lowliest pauper true pride in our ancient land. He left for Vvardenfell soon after it was opened to aid his brother in its settlement, and was a staunch proponent of Hlaalu interests in the island's colonization. The Echo offers its respects to his family and friends, though every loyal Dunmer in Narsis will no doubt mourn his death. It hopes that swift action will be taken against the perpetrator before they strike again. After all, if they are capable of killing a noble in his own house, then who and what else might be next?

MIR CORRUP SWAMPED

Mir Corrup, the once-famous resort town, is being threatened by encroaching toxic swamps. The sulphurous marshlands, having fouled the town's renowned hot springs, now jeopardize its trade hub status as well. Caravanners are already reporting difficulties transiting the Purple Road; Stuck carriages, swarms of insects, and collapsed infrastructure are all increasingly common. Llaros Samalsi, the governor of Shipal-Sharai, said he was working tirelessly to ensure a steady flow of cross-border trade. "We cannot change nature, but I am doing as much as possible to ensure travelers' safety along my part of the Purple Road." Hlaalu patrolling has been stepped up, and the governor personally took a trip to Narsis to discuss the situation with the Imperial Magistrate. His efforts have not been in vain, as prices of key trade goods such as flin, Colovian cheese, and marshmerrow pulp remained stable in the first quarter of 3E427.

ULVINI BALEN'S FINE CLOTHING

Need fine clothes in Narsis? Look no further than Ulvini Balen's shop in the Old Quarter. Our family tradition of timeless elegance ensures you'll always be at the bleeding edge of fashion, regardless of what's trending.

REDORAN RECLAIM IBBI-SUEN SILVER MINE -- TO WHAT END?

Recently, a contingent of soldiers from Ald Marak stormed the fortified silver mine of Ibbi-Suen, long held by a notorious local gang of defectors and bandits. In the aftermath of the assault, the most notable military action that the Waters March has undertaken in years, Serjo Delis Llethri -- Daughter of Redoran Councilor Garisa Llethri, and Commander of Ald Marak -- has promised to expand the scope of patrols throughout the region. The move, which would significantly bolster House Redoran's presence in the Coronati Basin, has prompted all outside observers to ask the same question: Why bother?

In general, the leadership of the Waters March have spent the Third Era -- and especially the last few tumultuous decades -- fumbling from one disaster to the next, slowly shrinking from the political stage as their more savvy peers take to the forefront. As their original purpose has become outmoded by the passage of time, House Redoran in the Coronati Basin have continually demonstrated an inability to govern in peacetime. Crucially, even their ability to respond to conflict has been eroded, as the initial loss of Ibbi-Suen mine demonstrated several years ago.

Even so, those who rule from the vestigial council seat of Ald Iuval refuse to accept reality, and stubbornly hold onto their dream of a resurgent Waters March. This seemingly bold development, then, can be contextualized as merely the latest in a series of delusional power grabs. Dying gasps from an institution flailing for relevance, desperately needing to be put out of its misery.

Does the reclamation of Ibbi-Suen mean bright things for House Redoran in the future? Probably not. But if it does, rest assured that they will find a way to squander it.

EDITORIAL: ART AND CULTURE IN HOUSE HLAALU
by Crassius Curio, Councilor of Great House Hlaalu
Vivec City, Vvardenfell District

Though a Cyrodiil by birth, I have been blessed to hold my seat on the Hlaalu council for many years. In that time, I have seen our Great House weather the tribulations of the time with a unique strength and determination. Indeed, our position is unique among the five Houses. House Indoril holds fast to the Temple, while House Redoran continues to arm itself for a war that will never come. House Dres was humbled by the Arnesian War, but rather than adapt to changing times, they still cling to their slaves and their crops, for they have nothing else. And the Telvanni magisters, as always, care little for what happens outside their fungal towers. After four centuries, Morrowind still remains, in the Imperial imagination, a second-rate backwater. While the other four Houses occupy themselves with their own concerns, only Hlaalu is left to build a prosperous future for this land as a true Imperial province.

Sons of our House hold the throne in Mournhold and the dukedom in Vvardenfell. The Imperial Proconsul holds court with us in Narsis. The Empire is the future, and so is House Hlaalu. Yet despite our clear mandate to lead Morrowind into a new era of commerce and collaboration, House Hlaalu continues to be weighed down by conservative ideologies. We could instead become a beacon of high culture in this province. With our influence, we can bring not only the material riches of the rest of the Empire to Morrowind, but the cultural riches as well. Breton sculpture, Khajiiti tapestry, Nibenese philosophy, the greatest works of the greatest minds in Tamriel could flow through Narsis like the waters of the Thirr, if only we let them.

And the flow will not only be inward, but outward. The austere beauty, the synthesis of natural and artificial that defines Dunmer architecture and stonecraft is beyond compare, yet almost unheard of in the western Empire. This is not only a shame for the outlanders who will never experience the vibrant cultural heritage of this land, but also for our own citizens. A thriving marketplace for Dunmer art and culture would not only enrich the people of this province, but enrich the spirit of every citizen beyond our borders. We have a choice to make. In the great conversation that is the Empire, the Dunmer voice has been silent for too long. It falls to House Hlaalu to speak up. And when we speak, shall we speak only in defense of the Dunmer coinpurse? Or shall we speak also in defense of the Dunmer spirit, the Dunmer mind, the Dunmer worldview? Let us redouble our commitment to the arts in Morrowind and we shall deserve the position which fortune has given us.

Editor's Note: A patron of the arts, Councilor Curio is himself a known and celebrated dramatist. Currently occupied with his latest production, any interested investors or collaborators are encouraged to contact Councilor Curio directly at his manor in Hlaalu Canton, Vivec City. The editorial board thanks Councilor Curio for his generous contributions to the Echo.

OUTLANDER NAMED HLAALU HORTATOR

In response to the increasing threat of the Blight, Hlaalu councilors on Vvardenfell have unanimously elected an outlander -- %PCName, a %PCClass of %PCRace descent -- Hortator of House Hlaalu. A Hortator, or House Champion, serves as commander-in-chief of the armed forces of a Great House. A Hortator has been selected only a handful of times by House Hlaalu since the First Era, and only ever during a House War. The most famous Hortator is, of course, St. Indoril Nerevar, who served as Hortator of the First Council. Rumors abound that the outlander bears the lost ring of St. Nerevar: One-Clan-Under-Moon-and-Star.

Hlaalu Councilor Velanda Omani shared with the Echo: "%PCName is a %PCRace of great determination and fine character. I am certain that they will conduct the office of Hortator wisely and well." When pressed for comment regarding St. Nerevar's ring, Councilor Omani said only: "Moon-and-Star is a sacred artifact of the Dunmer people. If it has been recovered, the Temple will say so." Representatives of the Tribunal Temple had no comment on this story.

At press time, the nature of the Hortator's role remains unclear, as does the effect of this news on Inner Sea trade. Several ships in the port of Bal Foyen were seen today offloading spirits and other luxury goods to make room for military equipment. We will publish supplemental editions as this story develops. As always, look to the Canyon Echo for the latest on trade, investment, and current affairs.

OUTLANDER WINS BIG AT CASINO

An Imperial man has -- to the surprise of all -- risen from rags to riches at the Narsis Fortuna Casino, traveling on the back of a stolen guar. According to the accounts of several credible eyewitnesses, the man "came gallivanting through the Market Quarter stinking and soggy," but when the outlander left the casino that evening, he was dressed "as if he'd found Orgnum's Coffer." When interviewed by a Canyon Echo reporter, the outlander identified himself as Vodunius Nuccius, and stated that he was a former resident of the colony town of Seyda Neen, on Vvardenfell.

"Stolen guar? Preposterous. I borrowed it and was then involved in an unfortunate accident that left me unable to return it! I don't even know how to ride the thing. Not to worry, though -- I have more than enough to pay for it now."

When asked how he had gotten so lucky, Nuccius responded, "I've had my share of bad luck. It was about time things turned for the good."

PROCONSUL AVIDIA MURDERED

Shock and horror in the Imperial Consulate of Narsis' Council Quarter, as Carasa Avidia, the Imperial Proconsul of Morrowind, has been found dead in her chambers. While the details of Avidia's death have not yet been revealed to the public as the investigation continues, the Echo has confirmed that the late Proconsul was murdered. Imperial officials quickly swarmed around the Consulate in the early hours of the morning, after a servant discovered the deceased; updates since have been few and far between.

Rumor, inevitably, has spread through the streets of Narsis, including bizarre and preposterous lies, such as responsibility falling upon House Hlaalu, an Imperial competitor across the border, or even the involvement of the heretical Sixth House cult. The Canyon Echo dutifully reminds all readers that the spreading of such unsubstantiated conspiracy theories is unacceptable, and that all citizens of Narsis should mourn this tragic violence.

While the details of Avidia's death have not yet been revealed to the public as the investigation continues, the Echo has confirmed that the late Proconsul was murdered. Imperial officials quickly swarmed around the Consulate in the early hours of the morning, after a servant discovered the deceased; updates since have been few and far between.

Rumor, inevitably, has spread through the streets of Narsis, including bizarre and preposterous lies, such as responsibility falling upon House Hlaalu, an Imperial competitor across the border, or even the involvement of the heretical Sixth House cult. The Canyon Echo dutifully reminds all readers that the spreading of such unsubstantiated conspiracy theories is unacceptable, and that all citizens of Narsis should mourn this tragic violence.

TEXT.old:
YET ANOTHER PROCONSUL MURDERED

"When will the chaos end?" Narsis asks, as yet another Imperial Proconsul, Galvus Pottreid, has been murdered within the Council Quarter Consulate. This tragedy follows the assassination of the previous proconsul, the late Carasa Avidia, and Pottreid's swift appointment to the position of the Imperial representative of Morrowind -- what does this mean for Imperial power in Narsis?

Imperial officials have yet to disclose information regarding the murder, though it is suspected that the two tragedies may have the same perpetrator, one with some kind of vendetta against the Empire. The city's Imperial citizens are in an uproar, with one resident stating "I'm afraid. If they can kill two Proconsuls, then nobody is safe!". It is currently uncertain if and when another Imperial Proconsul will be sent from Cyrodiil to represent Morrowind -- some doubt that Narsis will continue to be the home of the Empire in the province.

TSAESCI TACKLED AT CASIMOR

Surprising scholars and historians, a living Tsaesci has been found and killed within the long abandoned Second Empire stronghold of Casimor, nestled in the canyons of West Shipal-Shin. According to Master Micarya of the Fighters Guild, the Tsaesci "Qorinue-Najan" had been living in the ruin with its undead legion for thousands of years, and still believed the Four-Score War of the late First Era to be ongoing.

While remnants of the Akaviri invaders are not unheard of across Tamriel, the supposedly immortal Tsaesci are rarely encountered in the Third Era. Those which have been discovered were reportedly extremely dangerous. The Fighters Guild is to be commended for this feat of martial prowess, and its investors in Narsis will be pleased to see its reputation grow.

ISRAG TONG LEADER KILLED

Continuing Fighters Guild Master Micarya's rash bolstering of the Imperial institution -- the former leader of Andrethis' Israg Tong, Maren Othrenim, has been put down in the name of "taming corruption" within the guild.

Having stepped down as leader of the Israg Tong, Othrenim had joined the Fighters Guild in Andrethis and rose to the rank of Defender, becoming the guild hall's second-in-command. However, due to unsourced, so-called "corruption," he was struck down in broad daylight by a member of the Narsis Fighters Guild, who did not give him a chance to defend himself from accusations of illegitimate conduct within the organisation.

According to the Fighters Guild, Othrenim had been "manipulating the Andrethis Fighters Guild Master, covering up Hlaalu interference in guild politics." Such accusations are unfounded and the Canyon Echo stands to wonder why the guild would slander a man so accommodating to Imperial institutions and bureaucracy.

It is clear to many that Micarya does not seem to be stopping her misguided "war against corruption" anytime soon -- one must wonder what sinister motivations truly lie behind Master Micarya's brash crusade?

TEXT.old:
MAGES GUILD HEAD MISSING?

Despite fervent denial from the Narsis Foreign Quarter based Guild of Mages, Ysadora Bellette -- the outlander Arch-Mage of Narsis District -- has not been seen in some time, and is presumed missing. Suspicion arose as to the Arch-Mage's whereabouts after rumor got out that no resident mages of the guild hall had seen her at all in months; upon further questioning this source could provide no motive nor explanation for the Arch-Mage's disappearance.

"She's just on sabbatical for a little while, can't someone take a break in peace?", says Ralsa Ondusi, celebrity mage and second-in-command at the guild hall. Further inquiry by a Canyon Echo reporter resulted in their escorting out of the guildhall -- what does the guild know to be so guarded about?

While the Canyon Echo of course affords the Mages Guild every right to defend the status of Arch-Mage Bellette, in the name of truth and justice one must come to question the stability of the Imperial guild and its openness to justified questioning. Whether or not you believe the word of the Mages Guild (which we can neither confirm nor deny), this of course leaves the Canyon Echo -- and you, dear reader -- with one gripping question: where is Ysadora Bellette?

TEXT.old:
ARCH-MAGE RETURNS FROM AWRY EXPERIMENT

Arch-Mage Bellette of the Narsis District Mages Guild, who recently was declared as missing by the Canyon Echo, has suddenly and surprisingly returned to the guild hall after a long absence. Details of the Arch-Mage's original disappearance have not yet been revealed to the Canyon Echo, only that "an experiment of the Arch-Mage's simply went wrong and she was lost to us for some time. Rest assured that she has been recovered alive and unharmed by certain determined members of the guild, and regular operations will soon resume."

This comes not long after the guild vehemently denied accusations of the Arch-Mage's disappearance, telling Canyon Echo reporters that she was simply on "sabbatical." Though any official reasoning has not yet been provided, one has to ponder the details of the Arch-Mage's failed experiment and why it was so necessary to lie to reporters.

Though the Arch-Mage reportedly "needs to rest" and has not yet spoken to reporters herself, the guild's second-in-command Ralsa Ondusi has concluded that "this event should be viewed as a great fortune to the global magical community, as while there is still much work to be done before our findings can be publicly disclosed, the advancements we have made in the course of rescuing the Arch-Mage shall surely open the door for future discovery regarding lost spells and magical archeology."

TEXT.old:
ILMYNA HLAALU WITNESSES WESTERN MIRACLE

A ranking noblewoman of the Seventh Hlaalu Family and daughter to Belron Hlaalu, Ilmyna Hlaalu has shocked all as she and several others testify the witnessing of a miracle -- not one of ALMSIVI, but in the fashion of the western Imperial faith.

"I just can't explain it, I love the Three and I love my ancestors, but seeing it in person? It makes me reconsider where my faith lies, that's all I can say," says the young Hlaalu.

The so-called "miracle" occurred in the Chapel of Zenithar within the Narsis Foreign Quarter, where the ranking Imperial Cult priest Plutus Ceno and another cult minion of his invited Ilmyna Hlaalu to witness a rock (yes readers, a ROCK) that he had "seen in his dreams." Luckily for Ceno, this rock miraculously exploded into light upon the temple's altar, and left nine gems in its wake, seemingly signifying the Nine Divines of the Imperial pantheon.

Though Muthsera Hlaalu is said to now be actively supporting the Chapel of Zenithar and Imperial Cult in Morrowind, perhaps even converting herself, the Canyon Echo would like to remind its dear readers to not trust everything they hear, and that worship and respect of one's ancestors and the Three must always come first.

TEXT.old:
BLOODBATH BELOW BAZAAR

Rumor has practically exploded through the streets of Narsis about a total massacre within a gang hideout in the sewers beneath the city's Grand Bazaar.

It is currently theorized that the slaughtered gang members, believed to have belonged to the Camonna Tong, were deliberately attacked by a rival criminal organisation within the city. It is somewhat known that the criminal underworld of the Hlaalu capital, once kept only in the rational, native hands of the Camonna Tong, has since become oversaturated, and something of a tug of war between the Tong, the Empire's Thieves Guild, and the newly established Ja-Natta Syndicate, infamous for its new drug "Greydust". Whatever shadowy organisation could have gone to such drastic measures, however, is currently unknown.

"It's terrifying to think that such violence happened right beneath my feet -- that it can happen at any time," says one merchant at the Grand Bazaar.

Rest assured dear readers, that as long as you hold yourself in esteem and stay on the right side of the law, you have no reason to fear petty criminals -- we can all trust that the dedicated guards of the Canyon Watch shall protect us from all injustice.

BELT OF ST. OLMS STOLEN

Public outrage among members of the Temple as the famous Belt of St. Olms, an artifact once belonging to the saint of the Tribunal himself, goes missing -- presumed stolen.

Though the Eight-Bones Temple in Narsis, a popular pilgrimage sight and famously home to Vivec's spear Muatra, has reportedly tried to keep the disappearance of the artifact -- it being the temple's most revered relic after Muatra -- a secret, in order to covertly "reobtain" the belt, but this has so far been unsuccessful.

Now that the details of the theft have come out, the Eight-Bones Temple's Master Milara Orvayn has testified that "it disappeared in the hands of an Ordinator, one of our own and someone I trusted. It is likely this Ordinator has since defected and is doing Vehk knows what with the belt."

Additionally, Canyon Echo sources in Othmura down the Thirr river have heard rumor that this particular ordinator may have joined a cult of Mehrunes Dagon worshipers, and surely whatever they have stolen the belt for is due to malicious intent. Should this be true, Milara Orvayn and the Canyon Echo would like to warn readers that dangerous heretics of the House of Troubles should NOT be trifled with, and that the capable hands of loyal Temple warriors are putting in as much effort as they can to recover this historic, blessed artifact.

TEXT.old:
BELT OF ST. OLMS RECOVERED

Not long after the Eight-Bones Temple and the Canyon Echo declared the sacred artifact, the Belt of St. Olms, missing -- we are proud to state that it has been found and recovered without harm by the faithful of the Tribunal.

Indeed, as previously theorized via rumor in Othmura, the belt had been stolen by a traitorous Ordinator, who had joined a vile Dagonite cult deep within the large Daedric ruin of Naemunbatashpi. However, thanks to the valiant efforts of Master Milara Orvayn and her agents, the cult was rooted out from the infernal dungeon and the Belt of St. Olms returned to its display at the Eight-Bones Temple in Narsis.

The Canyon Echo would like to congratulate the Temple on this victory and on the sanctity of its blessed ways, for this clearly shows that, above all, trust, reliance, and faith may be found within the ancestors, and the Three.

TEXT.old:
EEC INVESTS IN CANYON OUTPOST

A western company notorious for its trade monopoly in Morrowind (for better or for worse), the East Empire Company has announced a new investment venture: a caravanserai trading post for merchants travelling along the Purple Road between Narsis and Nibenay.

Contracted exclusively with the Fighters Guild for protection, the "St. Ino's Caravanserai" is based out of a former small ranch belonging to a proud Dunmeri family -- what does this mean for the future of independent Dunmer trade with foreign merchants, when the Empire controls trade on both sides of the border? The EEC's refusal to contract a local Dunmer Tong or the proud Shinathi people of Shipal Shin, as well as the erasure of traditional familial agriculture can only mean one thing: the Empire's ruthless expansion both territoriality and monetarily will not stop, and it falls to hard working, dignified citizens of Morrowind to resolve this injustice.

While this may aid Narsis' economy in the short term -- EEC stocks rising at the Mesa Exchange as outlander excitement gets ahead of itself -- it is sure to poison the future prospects of the city and House Hlaalu should nothing be done to prevent these overzealous, expansionist western corporations.

ANCESTORS' ANGUISH REVEALED

Those troubled by the hostile spirits in the Foreign Quarter sewers, take notice. The Canyon Echo's intrepid reporting has revealed the reason for at least one of our ancestors' unrest: outlander influence. Having been given a chance to interview the most agreeable of the spirits, the Echo's source proceeded to coax out a tale of woe stemming from the elevation of non-Dunmer in society.

It is undeniable that the last few centuries have seen significantly increased foreign presence in Narsis. Citizens of all races may be found within its most sacred spaces and highest offices, while the Foreign Quarter itself has expanded from a small collection of farms into a thriving cornerstone of our city. To many of our ancestors, it must seem unrecognizable compared to the Narsis that they lived and died in.

Local Factor of the East Empire Company, Rogatus Cipius, had this to say on the subject: "The East Empire Company has the utmost respect for traditional Dunmer practices. In fact, we have just made a sizable donation to the Eight-Bones Temple to help resolve the ongoing situation."

The Canyon Echo reiterates its faith in Narsis' leadership to balance the material benefits of membership in the Empire with the spiritual benefits that come from proper respect for our ancestors.

ANCESTORS' ANGUISH REVEALED

Those troubled by the hostile spirits in the Foreign Quarter sewers, take notice. The Canyon Echo's intrepid reporting has revealed the reason for at least one of our ancestors' unrest: damage to the catacombs. In a sit down with the Echo's source, one of the more agreeable spirits revealed that several chambers of the catacombs have been flooded with sewage, disturbing the peaceful existence of all interred within. Most shockingly of all, the spirit cast blame on House Hlaalu and the Temple for failing to prevent this occurrence.

Whether or not this vitriol is directed at the proper targets is unclear, however. While it is true that Hlaalu officials recently ordered the expansion of the Foreign Quarter sewers, a spokeswoman for the House claims that measures were taken to ensure structural integrity, both of the sewers themselves and the catacombs they were constructed near. The issue, she suggests, may instead be a result of the Ja-Natta Syndicate's illicit activities within the sewers.

As for the Temple, Milara Orvayn, the master of the Eight-Bones Temple, took a decisive viewpoint. "The wellbeing of our ancestors has always been, and continues to be, our utmost concern. A project to undo any damage to the catacombs will begin as soon as we establish the sections affected."

TEXT.old:
ALTMER SHIP SINKS IN PORT

Terror on the Narsis Waterfront as the "Calaril Comet", an Altmeri tradeship, has suddenly exploded in the harbor, sinking into the waters of the upper Thirr. Having recently made the exhaustive trip to Morrowind from the Summerset Isles, the Beacon Company ship held many rare and exclusive goods from the far west -- unseen and unneeded in fair Morrowind -- now lost at the bottom of the port.

Authorities have concluded that the explosion was clearly an accidental mishap -- likely on the part of the Altmer crew. Though the representatives of the Beacon Company have refused to accept this clear verdict, all citizens -- especially those who frequent the Waterfront -- should rest assured that this momentary threat was swiftly handled and that nothing of the sort should happen again under the watchful eyes of our loyal Port Authority.

For the sake of public safety, the Canyon Echo would recommend that all dock workers secure their cargo tighter from now on.

GHOST TUSSLE AT GRAND TOMB

The Grand Hlaalu Ancestral Tomb, once a peaceful and reflective place of mourning and worship, has erupted into a battle beyond the grave as a Hlaalu agent faces off against the spirit of Ilvrin Hlaalu, a late noble of the Sixth Family who recently died in scandal -- disowned and caught up in vigorous anti-Camonna Tong ramblings.

In a tough battle within the sacred tomb, this agent valiantly put down the ghost and returned Ilvrin's spirit to peace with his ancestors. Though an unfortunate end for the feeble and troubled Hlaalu, the ability and mobilisation of our great and fair House should always be commended and celebrated -- the Canyon Echo would like to avidly thank House Hlaalu and this agent for their efforts.

TEXT.old:
FLASH CRASH OF EEC STOCK

Utter mayhem for a brief moment in Narsis' western-style Mesa Exchange, as East Empire Company stock falls to a devastating low and almost immediately rises back to a staggering high. Believed to have been brought about by a courier's announcement of current earnings (this information being devastating to EEC profits), the news practically brought a stampede to the stock exchange, with all shareholders quickly selling their stocks, leading to the mass fall in prices.

However, sharp and foreseeing as ever, House Hlaalu quickly used this mishap on the part of the outlander EEC and Mesa Exchange representatives, and swept up close to a hundred thousand drakes worth of stock. With stock prices rising high once again, the Hlaalu have once again cemented themselves as the most cunning and commercially successful of all in Morrowind and beyond.

EEC stock continues to rise and fall at a normal rate as before, though perhaps it would be wise on any discerning reader's part to take heed of such an event as this flash crash, and prepare for such opportunities in the future.

FLASH CRASH OF EEC STOCK

Utter mayhem for a brief moment in Narsis' western-style Mesa Exchange, as East Empire Company stock falls to a devastating low and almost immediately rises back to a staggering high. Believed to have been brought about by a courier's announcement of current earnings (this information being devastating to EEC profits), the news practically brought a stampede to the stock exchange, with all shareholders quickly selling their stocks, leading to the mass fall in prices.

However, sharp and foreseeing as ever, House Hlaalu quickly used this mishap on the part of the outlander EEC and Mesa Exchange representatives, and swept up close to a hundred thousand drakes worth of stock. With stock prices rising high once again, the Hlaalu have once again cemented themselves as the most cunning and commercially successful of all in Morrowind and beyond.

EEC stock continues to rise and fall at a normal rate as before, though perhaps it would be wise on any discerning reader's part to take heed of such an event as this flash crash, and prepare for such opportunities in the future.

TEXT.old:
HIGH HLAALU ABDICATES

A shock and a great blow to all loyal Hlaalu of Narsis -- and truly all of Morrowind -- as Athires Hlaalu, "Prince of Narsis" and former Grandmaster of House Hlaalu steps down from his position, retiring and moving on to (as an additional shock to the Temple faithful) "pursue the face of Veloth."

Patriarch of the Second Hlaalu Family, Athires championed and led our glorious house past the cruel outlander Armistice and into the burgeoning Third Age; under his mighty stewardship House Hlaalu grew and flourished, expanding north onto the sacred Black Isle of Vvardenfell and enterprising across all stretches of Morrowind. With Grandmaster Athires abdicating and a new leader of the House confirmed, it is unclear whether the future of our house is to be just as fruitful.

Most unprecedented of all, an outlander now commands our illustrious clan -- the new Grandmaster being %PCName -- a %PCRace. This outlander has been quickly rising through the ranks in the house, earning enough votes from various Hlaalu councilors to be rightfully elected as High Hlaalu, in addition to former Grandmaster Athires' consent. While many praise this new direction, others criticize Grandmaster %PCName, fearing that the house may become even more susceptible to Imperial influence without a strong, native patriarch to lead the house in the right, traditional direction.

Now, testified by the new Grandmaster, who apparently also was a witness to the event, former High Hlaalu Athires has left Narsis in search of Saint Veloth himself, after experiencing a vision of his face and supposedly sharing conversation with him. Though slow to accept this revelation, many in the Temple have agreed that these accounts truly are valid, as the former Grandmaster's visionary dreams were proved to be true as they foretold a kidnapped incarnation of a saint, who was then saved and sanctioned by the Temple. A new shrine built at the point of this saint's revelation to Athires, the Temple is said to be actively sponsoring former High Hlaalu Athires' search for the prophet Veloth.

Many now ponder the future of Great House Hlaalu, but we at the Canyon Echo can say with surety that for better or for worse, for richer or for poorer, native or outlander, no one can ever replace former Grandmaster Athires Hlaalu.

TEXT.old:
FIREBRAND ABOLITIONIST LEAVES NARSIS

All have breathed a sigh of relief across Narsis as infamous Breton slave abolitionist Cydne Jouarge has suddenly left Morrowind to return to High Rock. Jouarge had been harassing good, hard working slavers across the city and beyond, becoming one of the largest outlander voices of the uninformed, ill-willed "cause" in Morrowind and betraying the outlander's own armistice. Jouarge had even gone so far as to admit to the Canyon Echo that he had come to Morrowind in order to cause trouble, having somehow held correspondence with a slave here in Narsis.

Today, citizens can rest assured that the vile antics and treaty-breaking ravings of a madman shall cease, and that all just tradesmer are safe under Hlaalu stewardship. In fact, slave sales have only risen across southern Morrowind, Jouarge and his false "movement" having done more benefit than nought in the end.

TEXT.old:
MYSTERY POISONING UNDER FORTUNA

Investigators have been left baffled after the private rooms and office of the Narsis Fortuna casino were found filled with poison gas, its inhabitants -- several leading members of the Camonna Tong, the former owners of the establishment -- all dead.

The incident was first discovered when a merry gambler from the casino proper, just above the poison flooded offices, reported "a sudden dizziness, followed by a severe cough." The following expedition into the offices, still simmering with deadly toxic gas, resulted in the injury of one Hlaalu guard, who had inhaled too much; though thankfully they were able to be saved, and the room eventually cleared of poison by trained professionals.

Where the gas could have possibly come from is currently unknown. The new owners of the Narsis Fortuna, who mysteriously inherited it from the Camonna Tong and who wish to stay anonymous, have proposed that the incident was "a simple but unfortunate gas leak" and that "these things happen." Yet more disturbing, this mystery gas' particular alchemical origins cannot be deciphered by Narsis' best alchemists either -- "its substance is unlike anything ever seen -- on Tamriel anyway," they said.

Perhaps we, loyal citizens of Narsis and Great House Hlaalu, should simply allow the proper authorities to work and discover the cause of this tragedy, and in the meantime it would be wise for us all to mourn the unfortunate and brutal loss of a great many friends and kin in the Tong, taken from us by this strange poison.

TEXT.old:
RIVERKEEP ROBBED

"Theft!" Cries the Duke Fethas Hlaalu, as the Imperial-Hlaalu stronghold of Riverkeep is robbed of several rare and valuable items -- all by an unknown assailant.

"It was unbelievable!" Said one guard at Riverkeep, after finding the vaults noticeably less populated, "like it never happened! Only a few trinkets missing -- to my eye at least." While a proper inventory has not yet been taken, and the Riverkeep treasury is unable to surmise just how much has been taken at this time, it has been confirmed that several expensive Daedric throwing stars have been taken by the thief.

This thief -- whose identity the Imperial and Hlaalu guard are currently investigating -- should not be feared by the common citizen. It is important to recognize, dear reader: Should such a foul criminal of the highest dishonour strike again, our loyal and dependable Canyon Watch stewards are sure to handle it swiftly and efficiently.

"I will not be played. Not by some petty thief, mark my words," said Duke Fethas Hlaalu, furious at his wronging.

TEXT.old:
THE DEVIL DAGOTH UR DEAD

Many thought this day would never come, that the black scorn of the Blight and its cruel master, unjustly cast upon the fair Dunmer people, would never be rooted out of their cursed stronghold. This day, all people of Morrowind may rejoice at the sacred feats of %PCName, Saint Nerevar reborn and savior of all Morrowind -- perhaps all Tamriel -- as Dagoth Ur, unholy abomination and foul devil of the Temple faithful, lies destroyed forever.

After official recognition and sponsorship of the noble Vivec himself, the Nerevarine set about past the Ghostgate and into the treacherous, plagued stretches of Red Mountain on the isle of Vvardenfell. While exact details of the Nerevarine's heroism are currently scarce, it is said that they gathered several Dwemer relics -- long forgotten to uncursed mortal eyes -- and with this power the fated hero did what countless could not and struck down the putrid demon Dagoth Ur.

With the immediate dangers of Vvardenfell's Blight now gone, it is assuredly no better time to invest in the Black Isle's various ventures-- business booming on the recently-opened island. The Canyon Echo particularly foresees a rise in Dwemer and ebony exports, the rich area around the Red Mountain and its several ancient Dwarven cities now relatively safe.

On this sacred day, as the skies over Vvardenfell lay clear and blue, and the threat of the vile Corprus disease no longer lingers over us all, we must of course praise the excellent Nerevarine (to whom the Canyon Echo wishes to extend a personal congratulations) and, of course, the magnificent Three, who guided us in their infinite wisdom to this very joyous day; praise be to ALMSIVI, and the Nerevarine!

TEXT.old:
REVOLT IN BALMORA

The recent increase in the rates of tariff and tax by the Imperial administration was met with widespread condemnation across Morrowind. Traders and laborers alike abandoned their workstations to publicly protest what one port worker in Bal Foyen aptly referred to as "daylight robbery". Sadly, not everywhere did things remain civil. In the Vvardenfell city of Balmora, demonstrations soon descended into open violence.

As our frequent readers will know, since its reorganization as an Imperial district, Vvardenfell's economy has boomed, driven by the exploitation of its natural resources. As a consequence, however, its citizens disproportionately felt the weight of these new tariffs, targeting the islands' export focused economy. Tensions were running high and a small confrontation quickly escalated into a full-blown tax revolt, leaving four civilians and two guards injured.

We at the Echo would like to unequivocally condemn the violence and personally thank the local Legion commander, Larrius Varro, for restoring order to Balmora. Nevertheless, we feel it is important to properly confront the underlying cause of these disturbances and so would like to directly address the King Hlaalu Athyn Llethan.

Your Majesty, The Empire has brought progress into Morrowind, and with it prosperity to those who embraced the wonders of free trade. Yes, the times are not as easy as they once were, but sacrificing on our shared core values for momentary gain is not the solution, as the regrettable events in Balmora vividly demonstrate. Abandon these new taxes, and you will see how the natural flow of commerce fills the Imperial treasury much better than any tariff ever could.

TEXT.old:
GOBLIN ATTACKS CONTINUE

Locals report continued violence in the northern Shipal-Shin, as goblins descend the cliff sides in great numbers in near-nightly raids. Many are counted dead and even more wounded in the most recent assault, including several guardsmen and brave citizens in their daring defense against the cruel creatures. A tale all too familiar to our readers in these trying times.

An irate & wounded guard captain explains, "This isn't the first time we've dealt with this, but the number and fervor of their attacks has increased of late. They sneak close before jumping our night watchmen, and by the time we can respond in force, the goblins have already killed, stolen or burned their share before scattering and fading away into the night." Truly frightful for those involved, and greatly concerning to those who often travel the region.

In addition, many honorable traders have had their caravans ambushed and harassed at the hands of goblin hordes -- the foul beasts daring even to desecrate St. Veloth's holy path with these heinous crimes. The Echo encourages the wise reader to refrain from nightly travel while the attacks continue -- a night's safe rest is greater insurance for one's goods than risking an earlier arrival under threat of death and loss.

In search of reassurance, the Echo's reporters have reached out and received word from both the Imperial Legion & Fighters Guild that the issue is being looked into, and several independent contractors have taken part in the search alongside them. Let us honest-folk hope for a swift discovery and subsequent annihilation of the horrid hideouts of those responsible.

DRAVOS TURIL'S EXQUISITE GOODS

Next time you're in the Narsis Council Quarter on business, visit our store for the highest quality goods in all categories. Whether you're looking for a rare tome, fortifying alchemies, or enchanted ebony, we stock anything the discerning mer could require.

The Battle of Molag Beran
(Dunmer Traditional Ballad)

Did you come to hide from war,
Or come to herd the guar,
Or were you with the House Guard
At the Battle of Molag Beran?
For I was there, and fought and cried,
And tasted blood and thunder.
I stood in line with mace and shield
As Dunmer clan slew Dunmer.

The guard of House Retheran
Were bright arrayed for battle.
They came in pride, in columns wide,
But ran like frightened cattle.
We stood our ground on Tadras Banks,
Then turned their flanks and roweled them.
The field was bright with cousin's blood
Spilled by doughty Drenim.

We lost some gallant gentlemen
From ranks of brave House Drenim.
And many a wand'ring widow weeps
On the hills of Molag Beran.
Some fell for wrong, some fell for right,
All for the colors wearin',
And many bade the world good-night
At the Battle of Molag Beran.

TEXT.old:
Blood Beat

A beat.

The beat of the war drum,
The beat of heavy boots,
The beat of the heart,
Waiting for fate.

Glass sunlight,
Unyielding and cold,
Glinting and dancing
Across a metal sea.

The first wave breaks
The first blood falls
The first screams add
To the cacophony of noise.

Breakers leap--horses rear
Threats of thunder--cries of war.
Lightning shards--
Swords twist fatal dances.

Swords clash
And spears flash
The axe rends
Through heartblood.

Heat of hate
Heat of battle
Heat of blood
Steaming in the grass.

The fight for the field
Yields then charges
Back and forth
Pendulum of victory and defeat.

Second wave sweeps
Third wave struggles
Fourth wave brings
Fear and courage.

Bugle calls.
Hoards break from place.
Waves draw away
Shore prepares for final battle.

Heroes step forward,
Cowards run back,
The army thins,
The final struggle has come.

Fierce and determined,
Out slash silver weapons
Shields are thrown up
Bodies twist to avoid

Down comes the resistance
Up swarms the advance.
Walls crack,
Fortress falls.

Old flag is ripped down.
A new one flies in place.
Cheers block out
The groans of the wounded.

Army dissipates
Silence settles, cold and dead.
Black fly the carrion birds,
The smoke of corpse fires

Final sword is sheathed.
Final gasp is given.
Heads drop, others rear.
Last words are said.

TEXT.old:
Bralegel's Note

Dear sir,

I have little to report, save for a story of an interesting local character. I've already sent you the information about guard rotations, shipment schedules, and so forth; to date, things have not changed from the established pattern. Everything is as it should be, so the plans need no updating. I will try to sneak around and draw you a more accurate schematic of the place, but all in all, our plans should need little modification. So that this report is not a complete waste, I will now relate to you the tale as it was told to me by patrons of the local tavern:

When I took my seat, I noticed a very large Nord passed out among a stack of bottles. I did not imagine glass a comfortable pillow, and so I commented that someone should rouse him, or at the very least gently rest his head on the table. The locals advised me against this course of action. According to past history, the Nord would not appreciate it.

Though I could picture the Nord (they called him by the strange name of Kjohdor Elf-Flinger) being a vicious opponent in a bar fight, I asked about past experiences anyway. Believe me, sir, when I say it was not what I imagined.

Kjohdor was a mountain of a man, but the locals insisted that he was no fighter. Too lazy, they said. He was, in fact, a sorcerer, and a mediocre one at that. However limited he may be in that respect, though, he certainly gets the most out of his abilities. As they told me, one day it happened that a cocky Dunmer picked a fight with Kjohdor, thinking him a stupid, lazy brute. Ever the gentleman, the Nord took the fight outside.

While the Dunmer drew his sword, Kjohdor cast a powerful Feather spell on him. The elf laughed, thinking Kjohdor an incompetent. Then the big Nord made an obscene comment about the Dunmer's ancestors, which prompted the elf to charge him. With surprising grace, the Nord sidestepped, and picked up the rude Dunmer easily. Kjohdor then propelled the unfortunate elf into the sky with all of his considerable strength. About a hundred feet in the air, the Feather spell gave out, and the Dunmer plummeted to his death.

Sir, the man sounds like he might be useful in our endeavor, however, he might not be of a temper to follow orders. In any case, it is good to know of him, if only to aid us in steering clear of him.

Ever your humble servant,
Bralegel

Madness save me, madness take me!
Madness preserve me from madness greater still!
Chatter and chatter, night and day, day and night!
I have no rest, no quiet, not a piece of my own mind!
So much gold glitters before me, but I value the saint
and the one with mask is no saint!
Madness save me from my dreams!
Hide me, give me the peace of insanity!
I am drawn to the mountain,
but do not let me go!
I am drawn and quartered in faith
but I am loyal to the end!
Forgive me for hearing his terrible voice
even though I have scratched off my ears!
Forgive me for seeing his terrible dreams
even though I have torn out my eyes!
Forgive me for allowing him to infect my flesh
even though I still try to burn it away!
He wants me, to corrupt and taint
but I'm already touched by you, lord!
Sheogorath, I'm coming home to you!

TEXT.old:
A Defense of the Wolf Queen
Re-examining the Legacy of Potema Septim


A Greeting
Hail, friend! If you find yourself reading this, then we of the Wolf Shield Clan bid you fair winds and a full belly. We are a group of proud warriors and merchants from Haafingar, loyal to the Septim Empire and the people of Skyrim, and we invite you to read on and discover the truth about our maligned queen and the true heirs of Talos.

False Legacy
Over the past three hundred years, the usurpers' propagandists have worked hard to sully the memory of Queen Potema and her fair son Emperor Uriel III Septim. They paint a picture of bloodshed and strife, and the most daring even go so far as to question the righteousness of our queen's cause. But there are many throughout the Empire who remember the just reign of Uriel III and long for the restoration of the true Septim dynasty across Tamriel. It is our hope that by the end of this pamphlet, you, reader, will count yourself amongst our number.

True History
When it became known across the Empire that Kintyra, daughter of the sadly-inadequate Emperor Antiochus, was a bastard and ineligible for the throne, Potema moved quickly to protect the security of Tamriel and the legacy of Tiber Septim. Gathering a council of Imperial loyalists from as far away as High Rock and Morrowind, she and the true heir Uriel marched south to assume rightful custody of the Empire; the gates of the Imperial City were thrown open to welcome them and Uriel was crowned Emperor Uriel III Septim before cheering and ecstatic crowds.

But the unworthy Kintyra - despite the promise of clemency and protection from Potema - had slipped away before their arrival and sought refuge with her scheming uncles Cephorus and Magnus. Although none of these reprobates could command the loyalty of the Empire's subjects, their purses ran deep and so Kintyra's rebellion - the so-called "War of the Red Diamond" - began. Everywhere Potema and Uriel's armies travelled, soldiers flocked enthusiastically to their banners and swelled their forces, such that even grievous losses in battle could not diminish their strength. Unable to comprehend such glad loyalty, Cephorus and Magnus spread the rumor (one that regrettably persists to this day) that dark necromancies were the source of Potema's impressive numbers; proper historical investigation has found no evidence that anything of the sort ever occurred.

A Martyr of Talos
Although Kintyra was quickly captured and the Imperial peace restored to much of Tamriel, Potema's treacherous brothers continued to fight the forces of the Emperor and brought years of devastation to the lands they held. Finally, through deceitful words and bribes of unimaginable size, the traitors swayed the princelings of High Rock to their side, and honorable Uriel III was captured in an ambush far from the field of battle. The rebels wasted no time in murdering the true Emperor (it is believed that Magnus himself lit the fire beneath Uriel's carriage) and in so doing broke the line of succession that began with Tiber Septim's sacred founding of the Empire.

Potema, filled with grief and knowing that she was now the sole worthy heir of Talos, fought with redoubled fury but the tide of war began to shift against her. The coffers of Haafingar had been depleted by the civil works and reconstruction that she and her son had engaged in across Tamriel despite the war, whereas the traitors were rich from their looting and were able to buy ever more unscrupulous lords to their side until only Skyrim itself remained loyal to the Empire. This enduring loyalty is what drives those of us who follow Potema even today.

Legacy of the Wolf Queen
Potema and the people of Skyrim resisted the incursions of her brothers for ten years - a decade in which the stalwart righteousness of her lands stands in contrast to the misrule and anarchy of the rest of Tamriel - but the rebel forces had grown overwhelming and ultimately Haafingar fell to the traitors. The city was given over to one of their mad bastards, and from that point the Septim Empire began the decline that is so evident today.

But Potema was never found after the siege, and those who remember the goodness of her character and the worthiness of her offspring know that she is under the protection of the Divines. No doubt They plucked her from the harm her regicidal brothers wished and empowered her spirit to guard Haafingar - and, with our aid, the whole Empire - from the predations of these false Septims; this is why we continue to fight for the Wolf Queen and the restoration of Talos' true heirs.

If you have read this tract with a clear heart and been moved by our words, then we ask you to support the Wolf Shield Clan of Haafingar and Potema's loyalists across Tamriel. You can begin by passing this very pamphlet on to one you trust, and spread our message until the lies of the traitors are scorned rather than celebrated. Our time is soon!

By order of Uriel Septim VII, Emperor of Tamriel, and the esteemed members of the Elder Council

Let it hereby be known that the Elder Council, in the session of the 18th day of First Seed this year, has unanimously decided upon the abolishment of the 34th war tax, this tax having been instated in the year of 3E 401 in order to support continued pacification of the provinces in the wake of the perversions of the Simulacrum.

As peace and prosperity have henceforth returned to all quarters of the Empire, through the tireless vigilance of the noble Imperial Legions, it is now decided that the 34th war tax is to be replaced with a citizen contribution not exceeding 10 Septim per head of a household, for the maintenance of roads and watchtowers in these times of great need.


The Empire is Law,
the Law is sacred.

Come, brethren!
Let us wrest back our ancient rights from the avarice of greedy Hlaalu hands.
Too long have they annexed our territories, stolen our powers and mocked us in our trials.
We must unite - we must drive these foul usurpers from our most sacred lands and restore sanctity to our temples, shrines and tombs.
For too long they have haunted us on our very doorstep! Come, let us rid ourselves of this pestilence once and for all!
We rally tonight. The Hlaalu will pay for their insolence!

Signed

- Barys Hrothmalen
